findings.quoted_claim: Line-ruling z against per-map texture-preserving nulls spans **-1.30 to +5.94, median -0.27** across 69 scorable maps, against the human-verified control at **+25.6...+34.1**
findings.location: report/REPORT.md, Executive summary, deliverable 2 (line 21); repeated in the five-minute table (line 40: "vs the control's +25.6...+34.1")
findings.artifact_value: The corpus z values ARE correct (out/survey/corpus_analysis.json: min -1.30, median -0.27, max +5.94, n=69 — recomputed). The control anchor is not on the same statistic. analyze_survey_corpus.py line 150 HARD-CODES it: json.dump({"control_reference": {"ruling_z": [25.6, 34.1], ...}}) — the corpus screen never scored the control. out/survey/PROTOCOL_V2.md states it outright: "Run v1's own analyze() on the control map: z = +13.74 (prominence 69.33, null 12.73 +/- 4.12, period 4.39 mm). So under v1, the separation between known Greek letters and its worst false positive was a factor of 2.3. (The +25.6...+34.1 printed on v1's corpus_ranking.png as the control line was never computed by v1 - it was quoted from the validated battery, a different protocol, making that figure's reference line apples-to-oranges.)" Like-for-like separation is 13.74/5.94 = 2.3x, not the 4.3-5.7x asserted in sections/02_instrument.md 2.4 ("The control, on the same statistic, sits at +25.6 to +34.1 - 4.3-5.7x the corpus maximum"). Note verify_report.py's check passes only because it compares the report to the hard-coded constant in the JSON — the check is circular.
findings.exact_fix: Line-ruling z against per-map texture-preserving nulls spans **-1.30 to +5.94, median -0.27** across 69 scorable maps. Under the hardened re-run (protocol v2, 200 permutations with rim erosion and detrending) the corpus falls to **-1.20 to +4.64, median -0.09 across 71 maps, and the human-verified control scored under the identical protocol reaches +16.3 (empirical p = 0.005, 0 of 200 shuffles beat it) - 3.5x the corpus maximum, with 0 of 71 segments passing all five gates and the control passing 5/5.** (Do not quote +25.6...+34.1 beside a corpus z: that value comes from the validated battery, a different protocol. The screen's own protocol scores the control at +13.74.)

findings.quoted_claim: The four fixes are specified in §2.6 but have **not** been applied corpus-wide - re-running is free and laptop-only, and would tighten the reported corpus maximum (+5.94) substantially. Every corpus z in this report should be read as an optimistic upper bound on its own segment.
findings.artifact_value: They HAVE been applied corpus-wide. out/survey/corpus_analysis_v2.json (generated 2026-08-18 15:19:17) and out/survey/PROTOCOL_V2.md (written 15:27) implement all four prescriptions plus two more: config = {n_perm: 200, erode_fullres_px: 40, detrend_sigma_ds4_px: 90, min_cycles: 6.0, min_band_bin_index: 2, max_fwd_rev_r: 0.2}. Results: n_segments_scored 71, n_segments_passing_all_gates 0, gate_pass_counts {significance 4, cycles 19, autocorr 23, band_bin 23, fwd_rev 0}; corpus z_corrected range -1.199 to +4.642, median -0.085; the v1 flag z_dbg_gen_00166_inp_hr goes +5.94 -> +0.97 (p = 0.159); control w035 passes 5/5 at z = +16.259, p = 0.00498. REPORT.md was last written 2026-08-18 14:05:59 — 74 minutes before the v2 JSON landed. LOG.md's 2026-08-18 entry is titled "CORPUS SCREEN v2: all four FLAG_VERDICT fixes shipped; corpus re-scored; 0/71 survive". The report is stale, and it is stale in the direction that gives away its strongest result.
findings.exact_fix: 3. **The corpus screen as first run was under-powered, and we measured by how much.** It used 16 permutations per map and skipped the validated battery's rim erosion and detrending; on the one segment taken to 400 permutations the null's own standard deviation was 2.2x larger than the 16-draw estimate. All four fixes of §2.6 have since been applied corpus-wide (`out/survey/PROTOCOL_V2.md`, `corpus_analysis_v2.json`): at 200 permutations with 40-px rim erosion, sigma = 90 detrending and the three shape gates, **0 of 71 scored segments pass all five gates, the corpus maximum falls from +5.94 to +4.64, and the human-verified control passes 5/5 at z = +16.3 (p = 0.005).** What remains under-powered is the permutation test itself: at 200 draws the attainable p floor is 0.005, which both the control and one corpus segment reach, so the separation now rests on the shape gates (cycle count, autocorrelation, band-bin position, fwd/rev symmetry) rather than on significance alone.

findings.artifact_value: The AUCs are right but the attribution is not. out/ink9um_w035_scores.json gives 0.9991 (seed42) and 0.9982 (seed43) — verified. But sections/02_instrument.md 2.2 says those runs were on the PUBLISHED surface volume: "We ran ink_9um (seed42 and seed43, step-075000) on the published 28-slice surface volume (5820x5240 px at 9.362 um) in both z-directions." findings.exact_fix: The released `ink_9um` model reproduces the published w035 letters at **pixel AUC 0.9991/0.9982** on the published surface volume - an independent reproduction of that community result; our own tifxyz→surface-volume renderer, which is what makes the model runnable on scrolls with no published surface volume, reproduces that prediction at **r = 0.813** end-to-end from the raw scroll volume and independently recovers the 4.68 mm letter ruling.

findings.exact_fix: 11. **One statistic remains unexplained**: the ~37% of ink_3d firing variance left after fill, mean CT, z and winding radius (R² = 0.62) is not exchangeable noise - it carries real spatial structure (Moran's I 0.289 vs block null 0.213 ± 0.003) that no measured covariate accounts for, with regional CT texture/damage the most plausible untested driver. findings.quoted_claim: PHerc0139 produced no genuine air window anywhere (all candidates rejected by the gates) and carries the residual reference. ... The honest statement for 0139 is a bracket: SNR @ 0.25 somewhere in the ~39–116 range depending on reference and site; bandwidth ≥ 0.386, plausibly ≈ Nyquist.
findings.artifact_value: A genuine air window for PHerc0139 EXISTS in the project's own cache and PASSES the k2b gates. D:\vesuvius-data\trackD\qc_roi_PHerc0139_air2_128.npy (the audit's clean 128^3 window, origin [11936,4320,4608], recorded in qc/qc_k2_air0139.json as n128, l0_mean 50.02699518203735, zero-frac 0.0) run through k2b_detectability_index.validate_air with pap_mean_dn=126.7: mean_dn 50.0 < gate 63.35, flatness 24.6 < gate 40 -> PASS. Feeding that window as the noise reference to the SAME three k2b papyrus ROIs gives SNR@0.25 = 17.08 / 20.63 / 22.23 -> median 20.63 [18.85–21.43], and bandwidth 0.4364 / 0.4364 / 0.4619 -> median 0.4364 [0.4364–0.4491]. That is 1.9x BELOW the floor of the claimed ~39–116 bracket and would place the calibrator INSIDE the degraded tier (8.5–24.4), at rank 13 of 14 between PHerc0800 (20.08) and PHerc0257 (22.71). The 39x the report quotes is the audit's DIFFERENT single papyrus ROI on the same air window (I reproduce it: 38.59 vs the artifact's 39.13); the site-matched value the index's own ROIs give is ~20.6. The residual reference therefore inflates SNR@0.25 by 4.5–7.2x per cube (115.54/17.08, 148.14/20.63, 100.06/22.23), not by the ~1x-to-3x the bracket implies. Also: the k2b fallback candidates for 0139 were not rejected 'by the gates' — all 8 failed on coverage ('coverage 0.18–0.60, no clean sub-cube'), and the primary picker produced zero air candidates (no PHerc0139_air0/air1.npy exist). CONTROLS I RAN: per-voxel PSD normalization is size-independent to +/-7% at q=0.15–0.45 (128^3 sub-cube vs its 256^3 parent, tested on 4 cubes), so the 128^3-air-vs-256^3-papyrus comparison is valid — and the shipped pipeline already does this for PHerc0800 (64^3 sub-cube). Within-volume air-window PSD variability at q=0.25 is 0.89–1.13x on 4 of 5 scrolls tested, far too small to explain a 5.6x gap.
findings.exact_fix: §1.1, replace 'PHerc0139 produced no genuine air window anywhere (all candidates rejected by the gates) and carries the residual reference.' with: 'The k2b picker found no usable air window in PHerc0139 — its primary picker returned no air candidates at all, and all eight full-z fallback candidates were rejected for coverage (0.18–0.60 fill, no fully in-mask 64³ sub-cube) — so the shipped row carries the residual reference. A genuine clean air window in this volume does exist: the K2 audit's variance-aware search found one (128³, mean 50.0 DN, zero-frac 0, `qc/qc_k2_air0139.json`), and it passes the current validation gates (flatness 24.6). Re-referencing the index's own three PHerc0139 ROIs against it is the like-for-like measurement, and we report it in note (a).' §1.2 note (a), replace the final sentence with: 'Re-referenced against that clean air window — the same reference class the other 13 scrolls use — the index\'s own three PHerc0139 ROIs give SNR @ 0.25 = 20.6 [18.9–21.4] and bandwidth 0.436 [0.436–0.449]. The residual reference inflates mid-band SNR by 4.5–7.2× per cube. Across four papyrus sites on one common air reference (our three plus the audit\'s), 0139 spans 17.1–38.6 — so the honest statement is that PHerc0139 measures 17–39 on the same footing as the rest of the table, i.e. at or below the degraded tier, and its residual-referenced rank-2 placement is an artifact of the reference, not a measurement. We report the residual row for continuity but the anchor argument in §1.5 must not rest on it.'

findings.quoted_claim: - **Not a promise of readability.** The 0139 anchor is one-directional (necessary-class, §1.5). 0139 also had a segmented, rendered surface with human labels; the index does not measure segmentability or coverage.
findings.artifact_value: Direct answer to the scoping question: NO, the section never states the index as predictive of readability. §1.7 opens with 'Not an ink detector', §1.5 explicitly says 'readable-tier quality is *necessary-class*, not sufficient', and §1.4 frames the campaign result as 'observed correlation, not established cause'. That specific overreach is absent — the abstract correction is absorbed. What is NOT absorbed is the concrete, measured counterexample the project generated on 2026-08-18 and flagged in NEXT_SESSION.md §3 as 'The single most important NEW finding': the index's own rank-1 scroll, PHerc0813, produced 8 grown surfaces whose 5 on-material patches show lamella modulation 0.036–0.074 against the control's 0.443 (hunt/pherc0813_mesh_qc.json, tabulated in sections/02_instrument.md §2.9 and REPORT.md limitation 4). §1 never mentions this, while §1.4 simultaneously invites the index to be used as a target-ordering tool ('if a target list is being ordered by scan quality...'). A reader of §1 alone would order targets by this table; the project has already measured that doing so on rank 1 produced unresolvable sheets. Omitting the section's own strongest disconfirming evidence is the one thing a self-correction pitch cannot afford.
findings.exact_fix: Add a fifth bullet to §1.7: '- **Not a separability measure — and we have a measured counterexample.** PHerc0813 ranks 1 of 14 here. The first surfaces ever grown on it (§2.9) show lamella modulation 0.036–0.074 against the w035 control''s 0.443 — 6–12× less. High scan quality does not imply resolvable sheets; the two are different axes, and the index measures only the first. Ordering a target list by this table is ordering by where we can best *look*, not by what is there.'

findings.artifact_value: out/survey/PROTOCOL_V2.md §7.2, and the third control record in out/survey/corpus_analysis_v2.json (`w035_LABELS`): run on w035's own human ink labels — the ground truth itself — v2 returns z = +0.256, empirical p = 0.328, 3 gates of 5. PROTOCOL_V2 states it plainly: "**A handful of letters on an otherwise blank sheet would not trip this screen**". The screen passes the control only because the prediction map carries the model's dense page-wide response; the letters alone do not pass it. The section never carries this bound.
findings.exact_fix: Add to §2.4 immediately after the gate cascade: "One bound on this screen, measured rather than assumed: run on w035's human ink labels themselves — 13 letter components on a 54 mm profile — the same protocol returns z = +0.26, p = 0.328, 3 gates of 5. It is a page-scale test of the model's response field, not a letter-scale test. Sparse text on an otherwise blank sheet would not trip it; that regime is covered by the tripwire and the morphology battery, both also clean." Then qualify §2.7's bounded claim to "...would have flagged a page-scale ~5 mm ruling".

findings.quoted_claim: Five of eight patches (68.5 cm²) sit on scanned material  ... | PHerc0813, on material | **5** | **68.5 cm²** | 69–105 | **0.036–0.074** | −10, −10, −5, −2, +10 vox |
findings.location: sections/02_instrument.md §2.9, QC table and the paragraph under it
findings.artifact_value: Every per-patch value in that table except `area_cm2` is measured on a single 24×24-vertex window, not on the patch. hunt/qc_new_meshes.py: `WIN = 24`, "densest valid window of the mesh grid", and surface_mean_DN / surface_zero_frac / profile / peak_offset / contrast are all computed from `xs, ys, zs = x[sl], y[sl], z[sl]` — that window only. The script's own comment: "The grow step_size was 20 voxels, so a 24-vertex window spans ~480 voxels per axis". That is 23×20×9.362 µm = 4.31 mm per side = 0.185 cm², i.e. 1.35 % of each 13.7 cm² patch. The 68.5 cm² number itself is correct as an area sum (5 × 13.70, matching area_vx2 = 39,204 × 400 vx²), but the "on material" classification behind it rests on 1.35 % of each surface.
findings.exact_fix: Add a footnote to the QC table: "All columns except area are measured on the densest 24×24-vertex window of each patch (~4.3 × 4.3 mm ≈ 0.19 cm², about 1.4 % of a 13.7 cm² patch) — the window the depth-profile fetch can afford. 'On material' is therefore a spot check, not a per-patch coverage measurement; the two fully-empty patches are additionally confirmed at bbox scale (72 and 100 chunks returning 404)." And change "Five of eight patches (68.5 cm²) sit on scanned material" to "Five of eight patches (68.5 cm² of grown surface) spot-check onto scanned material".

findings.quoted_claim: on the control, reversing the render z-order destroys the map — fwd-vs-rev r = **0.076** ... (§2.5)  vs  "against the control's **0.055–0.094**" (§2.4)  vs  "against the control's 0.055" (§2.6)
findings.artifact_value: All three values are real and each has a source, but the section never says they are three different measurements of one quantity. out/survey/PROTOCOL_V2.md §2.4 spells it out: "control 0.055 (eroded mask) / 0.076 (verdict) / **0.0943** (recomputed here, common non-zero support)". Confirmed at source: salvage/verdict_consistency.json w035_s42__vs__w035_s42r r_pixel = 0.0764; verify_flag/vf_battery (FLAG_VERDICT) = 0.0552; corpus_analysis_v2.json control fwd_rev_r = 0.0943, fwd_rev_r_eroded_mask = 0.0552. As written, a reader comparing §2.5's 0.076 with §2.6's 0.055 sees two different 'control r' values with no explanation.
findings.exact_fix: Add once, at the first use in §2.4: "(The control's forward/reverse r is 0.055 on the eroded mask, 0.076 in the battery's full-resolution in-mask computation, and 0.094 over the common non-zero support — three masks, one conclusion; we quote the range 0.055–0.094 and the individual figure wherever a like-for-like comparison requires it.)" Then either use the range consistently in §2.5 and §2.6 or point back to that note.

findings.quoted_claim: Control: all three variants (two seeds + the re-rendered control) lock onto the same ruling ... z = **+25.6, +26.5, +34.1**  (§2.5 Test 1)  and  "independently passes the battery's ruling test (4.68 mm ruling at z = +34.1)"  (§2.3)
findings.artifact_value: The numbers reproduce exactly (salvage/verdict_periodicity.json: w035_s42 z 25.63, w035_s43 z 26.5, w035 rendered s42 z 34.1). But §2.6 line 165 of the same file now disowns them: "That older figure came from the validated battery's 5-draw null, and comparing a 400-permutation flag score against a 5-draw control score is the same apples-to-oranges error in miniature", and §2.4 line 100 says the +25.6…+34.1 control line "was never computed by v1 at all". out/survey/PROTOCOL_V2.md §6.1 shows the same control at 200 permutations is +16.3, not +25.6. §2.3 and §2.5 still present the 5-draw z values as headline evidence without the caveat the section applies elsewhere.
findings.exact_fix: Add a parenthetical at the first occurrence in §2.3 and again in §2.5 Test 1: "(these z values come from the battery's 5-permutation null; at 200 permutations the same control scores +16.3 — see §2.4. The period, orientation and cross-variant agreement are unaffected; only the z scale is.)"

findings.quoted_claim: spot-checked against `meta.json` it runs ~15–20 % high on well-covered meshes and far below on sparse ones
findings.location: sections/02_instrument.md §2.4, paragraph under the Scale-of-the-screen table
findings.artifact_value: I computed rendered-area ÷ meta.json area for all 77 rows with a cached meta.json. Well-covered PHerc1203 (gen 75, nonzero 0.57): ratio 1.186 for all eight — the only rows that match "15–20 %". Well-covered PHerc0800 (nonzero 0.37–1.00): 1.218, 1.271, 1.283, 1.290, 1.311, 1.386 — i.e. 22–39 % high. Small PHerc1203 patches: 1.51–1.81. PHerc1447: 0.39–1.42. So the stated band holds for one family of meshes only.
findings.exact_fix: Replace with: "spot-checked against `meta.json` it runs 19 % high on PHerc1203's well-covered meshes, 22–39 % high on PHerc0800's, up to 80 % high on the smallest patches (where full-resolution validity most exceeds the stored grid), and far below on sparse PHerc1447 meshes (0.39–0.92×) — which is the intended behaviour..."

findings.quoted_claim: For scale: the deep four-test probe of §2.5 covers ~28.5 cm² across two segments. **The corpus screen is ~15× larger**
findings.artifact_value: §2.5's own table gives 16.1 + 12.5 = 28.6 cm² (runpod/ink9um_runbook.md line 66-67: 16.10 and 12.53, sum 28.63). 28.5 is the figure from salvage/ink9um_1203_verdict.md ("~15.7 + ~12.8 cm^2"), a different measurement. Also note the ratio mixes units: 416 cm² is rendered area, 28.5/28.6 cm² is catalogued mesh area, and the report itself says rendered area runs high — 416/28.63 = 14.5×.
findings.exact_fix: Change "~28.5 cm²" to "~28.6 cm²" and "~15× larger" to "~14× larger", or add "(mesh area for the probe against rendered area for the screen, so the ratio is if anything generous)".

findings.quoted_claim: The 1203 maps are made of filaments 0.05–0.09 mm wide, 40–100× smaller than letter strokes
findings.artifact_value: salvage/ink9um_1203_verdict.md states two separate factors: "1203 filaments are ~7–10x thinner and ~40–100x smaller than letter strokes". 40–100× is the AREA ratio (letters area p50 42,363–43,264 px vs 1203's 365–1,032 px → 41–118×); the WIDTH ratio is 0.55 mm ÷ 0.05–0.09 mm ≈ 6–11×. Placed immediately after "0.05–0.09 mm wide", the 40–100× reads as a width factor, which would be wrong by ~5×.
findings.exact_fix: Replace with: "filaments 0.05–0.09 mm wide — 7–10× thinner and 40–100× smaller in area than letter strokes".

findings.quoted_claim: The re-rendered prediction correlates **r = 0.813** with the prediction on the published surface volume
findings.artifact_value: No JSON or script records this number anywhere in the repo — it appears only in prose (LOG.md line 253, NEXT_SESSION.md line 28, hunt/two_micron_path.md line 374, REPORT.md line 90). I recomputed it directly from the two primary TIFFs (out/ink9um_w035/w035_seed42-075000.tif, 5820×5240, and w035_rendered_seed42-075000.tif, 5819×5239, cropped to the common overlap): r = 0.8133 over the either-nonzero mask, which reproduces 0.813 to three digits. The number is correct. Two caveats: the value is mask-dependent (0.8865 over the full canvas, 0.8400 over both-nonzero) and the report does not say which convention it uses; and there is no script or JSON backing it, which is out of step with a section that cites a primary for every other figure.
findings.exact_fix: Change to "correlates **r = 0.813** (Pearson over the union of the two predictions' non-zero support; 0.89 over the full common canvas)" and add a one-line script (e.g. `report/scripts/verify_render_validation.py`) plus a JSON so the number has a primary, since REPRODUCIBILITY.md promises one for every claim.

findings.quoted_claim: any component with value > 195 DN (control blank p99) AND area > 10⁴ px AND width > 30 px triggers a mandatory human look
findings.location: sections/02_instrument.md §2.8 (and the same wording in §2.4 line 104)
findings.artifact_value: runpod/survey_segments.py line 63 examines only the twelve largest components per map: `big = [int(i) + 1 for i in np.argsort(sizes)[::-1][:12] if sizes[int(i)] >= 1e4]`. The report's "any component" is therefore "any of the twelve largest components ≥ 10⁴ px". Thresholds are also `>=` in code where the report writes `>`. In practice this is very unlikely to have hidden a hit (a 13th-largest component ≥ 10⁴ px would have to be the first to also clear the width gate), but the released tripwire is offered to the community verbatim.
findings.exact_fix: Change to "any of the twelve largest components in a map with value > 195 DN (control blank p99), area ≥ 10⁴ px and width ≥ 30 px triggers a mandatory human look" — or drop the `[:12]` cap in the script before release, since the section offers it as a copyable tool.

findings.quoted_claim: one pod, ≈ $0.35, 153–204 s per patch, 87–100 generations each
findings.artifact_value: The timings and generation counts verify exactly (hunt/pherc0813_meshes/*/meta.json: elapsed_time_s 153.3–203.9, max_gen 87–100). The $0.35 does not: LOG.md has no entry for the PHerc0813 growth run and no cost line for it; the only occurrence of that figure anywhere is NEXT_SESSION.md line 71, which is a forward estimate for a future run ("Grow surfaces on the next-best scrolls ... ~$0.35 each"), not a record of what this one cost. The other cost figures in the section do have primaries: $1.15 = $5.61 − $4.46 from LOG.md lines 213 and 248, and ≈ $5.5 for the survey from LOG.md line 356.
findings.exact_fix: Either add the actual pod cost to LOG.md's 08-18 entry and cite it, or soften to "one pod, under an hour of CPU time (≈ $0.35 at the pod's hourly rate)".

findings.artifact_value: Exactly right for the forward maps (out/survey/survey_all.json: 0.0324–0.2291, 0.0020–0.1828, 0.1105–0.3103) — and report/scripts/corpus_summary.py names the field `frac_gt_halfmax_fwd`. But the column header and the surrounding text ("no map is uniformly blank, none is uniformly saturated") refer to all 160 maps; including the reverse maps the ranges are 0.032–0.239, 0.002–0.191 and 0.110–0.353. The adjacent column is explicitly labelled "fwd/rev map r", so a reader has no cue that this one is forward-only.
findings.exact_fix: Change the column header to "half-max firing fraction (fwd)", or add to the paragraph below: "(forward maps; the reverse maps span 0.032–0.353 and are equally non-degenerate)".

sections.coverage_note: WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. (1) The file moved under me. 02_instrument.md was rewritten from the v1 screen to the v2 screen at 17:22 and edited again at 17:26 while I was auditing (REPORT.md at 17:23). Two findings I had confirmed against the 17:16 text were fixed by that edit and are NOT in my list (the §2.4 headline comparing the corpus to a +25.6…+34.1 control anchor "on the same statistic", and §2.8 item 2 listing the four-fix re-run as future work). Everything I do report, I re-grepped in the 17:26 file and confirmed still present. If the file has changed again, re-verify before acting. (2) ink_9um's training manifest — I relied on trackD/meta/ink9um_corpus.md's own statement that its 29-representation list "matches villa config aligned21_hybrid_3d2d.json"; I did not open that villa config or the HF bucket README to confirm the seed42/step-075000 checkpoint was trained on that exact manifest. The finding is strong (w035 is listed in both training splits and is absent from the three named validation segments) but the confirming document is the project's own scouting note, not the upstream config. (3) The unique-surface count cannot be settled from local data: three PHerc1203 rows never re-downloaded (hunt/out/corpus_valid.json shows EndpointConnectionError for auto_grown_20250923163217042 / …163219195 / …163223390), so the true SHA-based total over all 80 rows is somewhere in 66–69 and only a re-fetch can close it. (4) No figure PNG was opened; I verified only that every figure path resolves (verify_report.py check 1 passes). I did not check whether corpus_ranking.png / corpus_screen_v2.png actually depict what their captions claim, and note that PROTOCOL_V2 says corpus_ranking.png's control reference line is apples-to-oranges — §2.4 no longer cites that figure but §2.6's and §2.9's figures were not visually inspected. (5) S3 claims not tested against the live bucket: "three GP scrolls have a segments/ prefix", "the six best-scanning GP volumes have no segments/ prefix", "PHerc0813 has never had a published surface", and the 8.64 µm / 9.362 µm volume pairings. (6) Cost figures beyond $1.15 and ≈$5.5 have no billing artifact ($0.35 growth, $0.70 render estimate, $0.20 PHerc0800 re-render). (7) I did not re-run the 200-permutation v2 screen or the 400-permutation flag verification; I verified their outputs against their JSONs and recomputed all derived statistics (quantiles, gate counts, Spearman, ratios) from those JSONs. (8) §2.1's model description (~34 M parameters, 17×128×128, fp16, all 14 checkpoints mode:"flat") was taken from runpod/ink9um_runbook.md; no checkpoint file was opened. (9) One thing I deliberately did NOT chase to ground: the same PHerc1203 segment name renders to 16.1 cm² in the §2.5 probe (runbook) and 0.90 cm² in the corpus survey (survey_all.json, canvas 1239×1239), with hunt/corpuscache/…/meta.json recording max_gen 30 / 0.597 cm² while hunt/geometry_compare.md describes the same name at 198 generations. That is consistent with the S3 republishing §2.7 already flags, and it does not make any reported number wrong (both figures are correctly sourced), but it means "the segment we probed" and "the segment we screened" may be different objects under one name. Worth one sentence in §2.5 if Ben wants to pre-empt the question.

findings.quoted_claim: residual translation between the two reconstructions measured at 0.017 voxel, below the pre-set 0.05-voxel gate, so no resampling was applied
findings.location: sections/03_screens.md §3.2, second bullet (and §3.1: "All four blockers were fixed before the full screen ran")
findings.artifact_value: The string "0.017" as a translation appears in exactly one place in the whole project: a comment on line 6 of the k3_stage2_screen.py docstring ("sub-voxel translation check (skip shift if <0.05 vox — measured 0.017)"). No code computes it. `grep -rn "phase_cross_correlation|upsample_factor" --include=*.py` returns zero hits outside hunt/. k3_stage2_screen.py loads both L1 arrays and never registers them. out/k3_s2_stats.json has no alignment field. The only alignment measurement that exists anywhere is stage-1's integer-level L3 phase correlation (out/k3_stage1_stats.json: shift_110_rel_74_voxels [0,0,0], phase_corr_peak 0.163) — and qc/k3_stage1_review.md B4 states that this "constrains residual translation only to ±0.5 L3 voxel = ±4 full-resolution voxels" and demands "sub-voxel registration ... at the target level and report residuals". The "pre-set 0.05-voxel gate" likewise appears nowhere but that same comment. out/k3_sensitivity_bound.md caveat 5 hedges correctly ("Alignment is validated to sub-voxel only at the tested level"), but §3.2 states it flatly as verified with a number. This also underpins §3.4: sub-voxel edge-profile mismatch is exactly the PSF-striping mechanism, so an unverified sub-voxel residual is not separable from it.
findings.exact_fix: Replace the bullet with: "**Alignment: integer-level only, volumes used native.** Stage-1 phase correlation at L3 returned shift (0,0,0), which bounds residual translation to ±4 L0 voxels; no sub-voxel registration was run at L1, and no resampling was applied (resampling would have blurred the 74/110 ratio at sheet boundaries — the thing being measured). QC blocker B4 is therefore mitigated, not closed: per-voxel ratio integrity at sheet boundaries inherits that residual, and it is not separable from the PSF-mismatch striping of §3.4." Correspondingly change §3.1's "All four blockers were fixed" to "Three blockers were fixed and the fourth (alignment) is mitigated but not closed — see §3.2." Alternatively, run and archive a sub-voxel registration at L1 and cite its output file.

findings.quoted_claim: A Gaussian 4σ tail on that n predicts ~8,488 hits; observing 2 means the detrended statistic is strongly sub-Gaussian in its left tail. ... 2 hits against a Gaussian expectation of ~8,488 is a direct measurement that the detrended-ratio statistic and its threshold produce essentially zero false positives at scroll scale
findings.location: sections/03_screens.md §3.3 para 1 and §3.3 numbered point 1 (also REPORT.md exec summary bullet 4)
findings.artifact_value: The arithmetic is right but the denominator is not matched to the numerator. 2.68e8 × Φ(−4) = 8,487.9 — reproduces exactly (out/k3_sensitivity_bound.json fpr.gaussian_expected_at_4sigma = 8488, n_tested_approx = 2.68e8). But k3_stage2_screen.py lines 130–131 fire the channels as `good & cobright & (det < -4*sigma)`: a voxel can only fire if it ALSO passes co-brightness (both energies above papyrus p75). The observed "2" is a post-gate count; the 8,488 is a pre-gate expectation. I re-ran the exact stage-2 pipeline on the cached L1 arrays (8 contiguous 64-slice blocks, 464 slices, 3-voxel erosion, same offsets and p75 gates — my run reproduced air_offset_74keV, air_offset_110keV, p75_74 and p75_110 to full float precision): aggregates with den≥14 extrapolate to 2.63e8 (confirming ~2.7e8, and closing the memo's own open item "was not re-derived from the L1 arrays here"), but only 20.3% of them pass the co-brightness gate (per-slab range 18.2–25.4%), i.e. 5.3e7 eligible. Matched Gaussian 4σ expectation = 5.3e7 × Φ(−4) = ~1,690 (range ~1,520–2,120), not 8,488 — the quoted figure is inflated 5.0×. The ungated <−4σ count was never computed by the script, so the sub-Gaussian inference cannot be made against the ungated n at all. The conclusion (essentially zero false positives; strongly sub-Gaussian left tail) survives unchanged: 2 vs ~1,690 is still ~800×.
findings.exact_fix: §3.3 para 1: "**Result: 2 singleton voxels fired.** The screen evaluated ~2.63×10⁸ aggregates with den ≥ 14 (re-derived from the L1 arrays); firing additionally requires co-brightness, which 20.3% of those aggregates pass, so ~5.3×10⁷ were eligible to fire. A Gaussian 4σ tail on that eligible n predicts ~1,690 hits; observing 2 means the detrended statistic is strongly sub-Gaussian in its left tail." §3.3 point 1: "2 hits against a matched Gaussian expectation of ~1,690". REPORT.md exec summary: "(2 voxels in 5.3 × 10⁷ eligible aggregates against a Gaussian expectation of ~1,690)".

findings.quoted_claim: **5/28 null windows ≥ 1.43**, and two windows on the same ring and z as #3 reach 1.52 — above both flagged values. A pre-selected top-cluster window sitting at ~p80 of its own matched base rate is nothing.
findings.artifact_value: Everything except "~p80" checks out exactly against comb/comb_skeptic_k3.json null_summary (min 1.1704, p25 1.2618, p50 1.3243, p75 1.3846, max 1.5238, n_null_ge_1p43 = 5; the two 1.52 windows are both kind "#3_ring" at z=3925). But the clusters themselves sit higher than p80. Sorting the 28 med_seq values against cluster_medians_seq: #3 = 1.4813 is exceeded by only 2 of 28 nulls → 92.9th percentile (empirical one-sided p = 3/29 = 0.103); #5 = 1.4648 is exceeded by 4 of 28 → 85.7th percentile (p = 5/29 = 0.172). "~p80" is the percentile of the 1.43 threshold (23/28 = 82.1%), not of the flagged values. The conclusion still holds — neither is significant, and the windows were pre-selected as top stage-2 clusters, which biases them high by construction — but the stated number understates the clusters' standing by roughly a decile in the direction that favours the report's own refutation.
findings.exact_fix: "...— above both flagged values. The flagged windows sit at the 86th (#5) and 93rd (#3) percentile of their own matched base rate — empirical one-sided p = 0.17 and 0.10 on n = 28 — and they were pre-selected as the top stage-2 clusters, so that placement is what selection alone predicts." (Same correction applies to comb/COMB_VERDICT.md flag 6, which is where "~p80" originates.)

findings.quoted_claim: The residual ~36% of variance retains genuine spatial structure (Moran's I = 0.289 vs block null 0.213 ± 0.0025, z = +31; top-1% residual tiles cluster at mean NN 2.10 vs 2.39 ± 0.06 block null)
findings.artifact_value: Two different models are spliced. The Moran's I = 0.289 / block null 0.213 / NN 2.10 vs 2.390 figures are all the M1 residual from salvage/scalar_report.md §4, and M1's R² = 0.621 (also quoted three sentences earlier in the same paragraph as "R² = 0.62") — so its residual is 1 − 0.621 = 37.9%, i.e. ~38%. The "~36%" comes from a different model: salvage/reframe_correlations.json R2_f05_all_proxies = 0.63456 → 36.5% (reframe_report.md §2 says "The residual ~36% retains spatial structure"), which adds ct_std/surf_frac/surf_recovery on top of the four covariates. As written, "R² = 0.62" and "the residual ~36%" cannot both be true of the same field.
findings.exact_fix: "The residual ~38% of variance retains genuine spatial structure (Moran's I = 0.289 ...)" — or, to keep the 36% figure, "Adding the texture and surface proxies raises the ceiling only to R² = 0.635; the residual ~36% still retains genuine spatial structure (M1 residual Moran's I = 0.289 ...)".

findings.quoted_claim: The HIGH channel fired on **51,343 voxels in 30,258 clusters**
findings.artifact_value: 51,343 is in out/k3_s2_stats.json (high_channel_voxels = 51343) and reproduces. 30,258 is in no artifact. k3_stage2_screen.py computes the cluster count at line 139 (`lab, n = ndimage.label(ch)`) and only *prints* it (line 150); nothing writes n to disk. out/k3_s2_high_clusters.json holds only the top 25 rows, and the binary masks lowm/highm are in-memory only, so the number cannot be recomputed from any saved output. `grep -rn "30258|30,258"` across the whole tree hits only LOG.md line 128 (the project chronology, transcribed from that stdout print) and the report section itself.
findings.exact_fix: Either (a) cite the provenance honestly — "51,343 voxels in 30,258 clusters (voxel count `out/k3_s2_stats.json`; cluster count from the stage-2 run log, `LOG.md` 2026-08-16 — the labelled mask was not persisted)" — or (b) drop the cluster count and write "fired on **51,343 voxels**, dominated by a few dozen compact clusters (top 25 in `out/k3_s2_high_clusters.json`)", or (c) re-run the labelling step and save the count.

findings.quoted_claim: blur the 110 keV channel with a small Gaussian and find the σ that minimizes the 4σ-excess population. At σ_eq = **0.62 px (#3)** and **0.56 px (#5)** the hot-voxel count collapses **5220 → 958 (5.4×)** and **3477 → 967 (3.6×)**
findings.artifact_value: Two problems, and the method description understates the evidence. (1) σ_eq was NOT found by minimising the excess population — comb/comb_k3_psfmatch.py `estimate_sigma_eq()` derives it independently from the in-plane radial PSD ratio (docstring line 14: "the true blur mismatch sigma_eq from the in-plane radial PSD ratio"; results sigma_eq_px 0.624 / 0.557), and the sweep was then run to test whether the collapse occurs at that predicted σ (comb_k3_psfmatch2.py: "if the excess load collapses at sigma ~ sigma_eq (0.56-0.62 px from the PSD fit) ... artifact"). As written the test reads as post-hoc tuning; it is a pre-registered prediction, which is stronger. (2) The #5 numbers are all measured at σ = 0.62, not 0.56 — comb/k3_psfmatch2.json #5 has grid points {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.62, ...} and 0.56 is not among them; n_hot 967 / largest 39 / elongation 4.47 are the s0.62 entries (at σ = 0.5 the values are 948 / 43 / 5.39). Ratios recompute correctly: 5220/958 = 5.45 → "5.4×"; 3477/967 = 3.60 → "3.6×"; #3 555→103 vox, 16.86→11.65 elongation and #5 163→39, 7.65→4.47 all match. Also unreported: comb/k3_psfmatch3_controls2.json shows an ordinary papyrus control window at (3600,1058,989) collapsing 11,196→1,374 (8.1×) under the same blur — independent support that the excess is a global PSF artifact, not specific to #3/#5.
findings.exact_fix: "The quantitative test (`comb/comb_k3_psfmatch*.py`, `comb/k3_psfmatch*.json`): the blur mismatch is estimated independently from the in-plane radial PSD ratio at σ_eq = **0.62 px (#3)** and **0.56 px (#5)**, then the 110 keV channel is blurred across a σ sweep to test whether the 4σ-excess population collapses there. At the matched blur (σ = 0.62 px, the nearest sweep point to both estimates) the hot-voxel count collapses **5220 → 958 (5.4×)** and **3477 → 967 (3.6×)**, and the elongated streak components shrink and de-elongate (largest component #3: 555 → 103 vox, elongation 16.9 → 11.7; #5: 163 → 39 vox, 7.7 → 4.5). Matched control windows on ordinary papyrus collapse the same way (up to 8.1×, `comb/k3_psfmatch3_controls2.json`) — the effect is global to the scan pair, not a property of these clusters."

findings.quoted_claim: **Hard negatives are sheet surfaces, not cracks.** The FP mode is painting *intact* sheet surfaces (79% membranes, 0.2% crack ribbons; firing *anti*-correlates with damage at ρ = −0.54).
findings.artifact_value: The §3.8 lead-in does carry the caveat properly ("63 sampled probability maps ...; sample explicitly top-pmax/edge-biased — rates below characterize the sampled morphology, not unbiased scroll-wide rates") — so within §3.8 the requirement is met. §3.11 item 1 is the leak: it restates 79% and 0.2% as unqualified properties of "the FP mode", in the section a stranger will lift as the recipe. salvage/morph_report.md is emphatic that this is not licensed: "The sample is top-pmax biased and therefore EDGE-biased: median sampled tile sits at the 98.8th percentile of fleet pmax but only the 4.4th percentile of fleet f05; 29/63 tiles have fill < 0.2 ... All population rates below are conditional on this biased draw of n≈60". The denominator is also narrower than "fired voxels": it is voxels in the 352 connected components ≥20 vox across 63 tiles (79% is the share in components ≥2000 vox; the blob-class voxel share is separately 0.786). Both figures verified against morph_report.md's census table. Note ρ = −0.54 is NOT from the biased sample — it is the full 29,748-tile reframe result — so mixing the two in one parenthesis compounds the impression that all three are scroll-wide.
findings.exact_fix: "**Hard negatives are sheet surfaces, not cracks.** In the §3.8 morphology sample (63 top-pmax/edge-biased tiles — sampled-morphology rates, not scroll-wide rates) 79% of fired voxels sit in thin sheet-conformal membranes and only 0.2% in through-sheet crack ribbons, and across all 29,748 tiles firing *anti*-correlates with damage at ρ = −0.54."

findings.quoted_claim: This refutes the entire input-side intensity-adaptation family (histmatch, mean/std alignment, percentile tweaks) in one experiment: the domain shift lives at texture/morphology level.
findings.location: sections/03_screens.md §3.9, "The controlled test" paragraph (and §3.11 item 2: "Input-side intensity adaptation is refuted")
findings.artifact_value: The experiment itself is clean and genuinely matched — qc_live/qc_histmatch_result.json: same tile (7424,7168,11776), same checkpoint, same pod, f05 0.03924 → 0.08105 (ratio 2.066, so "doubled" is fair), matching verified (matched_p [25, 96, 154.2] vs tgt_p [26, 97, 155]), and the baseline 0.03924 independently reproduced on the laptop in qc_norm_equiv_result.json. The Paris 4 comparator 0.06952 is the same-pipeline in-domain ink-active value, so "exceeding the in-domain ink-active level (0.0695)" is the right apples-to-apples comparison. The problem is n = 1 tile. That is disclosed in the §3.7 scorecard ("single 256³ tile") but not in §3.9 or §3.11, where the result is generalised to an entire family of methods. round1_verdict.md makes the same leap. Nothing in the artifacts tests mean/std alignment or percentile tweaks at all.
findings.exact_fix: "On this single 256³ tile, giving 1203's texture Paris 4's intensity profile makes it look *more* Paris4-ink-like to the model — the opposite of the intended effect. One tile is not a proof for the whole input-side family, but it removes the cheapest member of it (histogram matching) and points the same way as the morphology evidence: the domain shift lives at texture level, not intensity level." §3.11 item 2: "Input-side intensity adaptation looks unpromising (f05 doubled under verified histogram matching on the one tile tested, §3.9)."

findings.quoted_claim: (a) produce silent tiles on 1203 (the in-domain signature: 5/8 random Paris 4 blocks at f05 = 0.000 vs 0 silent tiles in 29,748 here)
findings.artifact_value: The numbers are exact — qc_paris4_result.json block_f05 = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0817, 0.0, 0.0042, 0.0226, 0.0, 0.0] (5 zeros of 8), pct 90 = 0.0118 → "p90 = 0.012"; and I confirmed 0 silent tiles from tiles.parquet directly (29,748 scored rows, f05 min = 0.00176, zero rows below 1e-6). But the two sides are not comparable, and §3.11 freezes this as an acceptance gate a stranger must meet. Reading qc_live/qc_paris4.py: the 8 Paris 4 blocks are 64³ blocks drawn with `rng.integers(s//4, 3*s//4)` from the released zarr's own array bounds (shape 75784×32693×32693), i.e. ~154 µm cubes sampled from the array's middle half with NO material/mask gating. A 1203 "tile" is a mask-gated 256³ L0 tile ≈ 615 µm — 64× the physical volume — so it is 64× more likely to contain at least one firing voxel before any model difference. The 5 "silent" blocks have pmax 0.016/0.008/0.012/0.0/0.337, consistent with landing outside material rather than with confident in-material quiet (round1_verdict.md calls them "interior" blocks, which the code does not enforce). n = 8 vs n = 29,748. The conclusion is separately and properly supported by control 5A, which IS matched (fleet pipeline on Paris 4 256³ tiles: ink-active 0.0695, quiet 0.0282, vs 1203 median 0.0645).
findings.exact_fix: "(a) produce silent tiles on 1203 — measured on volume-matched, mask-gated 256³ tiles, since the 5/8-silent Paris 4 figure of §3.7 comes from unmasked 64³ blocks (1/64 the volume) and is not a like-for-like comparison; the matched in-domain reference is control 5A, where the same pipeline on Paris 4 gives f05 0.0695 in an ink-active tile and 0.0282 in a quiet one, against a 1203 median of 0.0645 and a floor of 0.0018 over all 29,748 tiles".

findings.quoted_claim: There is no Pb-signature anomaly anywhere in the screened scroll, including the title region.
findings.artifact_value: "anywhere in the screened scroll" is supported (the screen is full-volume at L1). "including the title region" is not: no artifact locates the Paris 4 title region, and nothing verifies it survived the 3-voxel mask erosion, the den≥14 aggregation and the co-brightness gate. `grep -rn -i "title region"` across trackD returns only LOG.md lines 50 and 127 — the project chronology, not a measurement. This is also the worst place to make the claim: the title sits on the outermost surface, exactly where §3.3 and §3.5 concede the screen is weakest ("the p75 co-brightness gate ... specifically disfavors the partial-volume-dimmed sheet-surface voxels where ink lives, flooring sensitivity at ≈ 70–170 µg/cm²"), and my L1 measurement shows the gate discards ~80% of papyrus aggregates.
findings.exact_fix: Either drop the clause — "There is no Pb-signature anomaly anywhere in the screened volume." — or substantiate it: "...anywhere in the screened volume. The screen covers the full L1 volume, so the title region is included; note however that outer-surface voxels are the ones the erosion and co-brightness gates cut hardest (§3.5 (iv)), so coverage there is nominal rather than demonstrated."

findings.quoted_claim: bulk on/off-sheet ratio 0.64–1.62
findings.location: sections/03_screens.md §3.7, scorecard row 2 (repeated as §3.11 item 1 corollary: "bulk on/off-sheet contrast 0.64–1.62×")
findings.artifact_value: Recomputed from qc_live/qc_morph_result.json: 21 of the 27 tiles have usable on/off-sheet f05. The range 0.64–1.62 is exactly reproduced, but only over the 5 tiles with frac_interior == 1.000 (0.64, 0.92, 1.45, 1.55, 1.62). Widen "bulk" by a hair to frac_interior ≥ 0.9 and the range becomes 0.64–3.44: tile w0_prob_0_11776_9984 has frac_interior 0.906, 52,783 on-sheet voxels and a ratio of 3.44. round1_verdict.md dismisses the 3–15× tiles as "all low-fill fragments where the sheet support is tiny (down to 85 voxels)" — that description does not fit this tile. The report quotes the range with no n and no definition of "bulk", and §3.11 turns it into an absolute ("on-sheet gating in post-processing can never rescue this output").
findings.exact_fix: "bulk on/off-sheet f05 ratio 0.64–1.62 across the 5 fully-interior tiles of 27 (0.64–3.44 if the cut is relaxed to ≥90% interior)", and soften §3.11 to "on-sheet gating in post-processing is very unlikely to rescue this output — the FPs are already on-sheet, and sheet contrast in fully-interior tiles is 0.64–1.62×".

findings.quoted_claim: 36% of dense voxels within 2 voxels of the mask edge vs 1.0% of papyrus — a 37× over-representation
findings.artifact_value: Faithfully transcribed from qc/k3_stage1_review.md B2, which says "36% of dense voxels lie within 2 voxels of the mask edge (papyrus overall: 1.0% — a 37× over-representation)". But 36 / 1.0 = 36.0, not 37. The underlying unrounded values are not in any JSON (out/k3_stage1_stats.json has no edge-distance fields), so the ratio cannot be recomputed — the error is inherited from the QC memo. Every other number in this sentence checks out exactly against out/k3_stage1_stats.json: dense_ratio_median 1.7051 → "1.705", ratio_median 1.2484 → "1.248", dense_voxels 3196, papyrus_voxels 4790408; and "selecting on the denominator instead gives 1.46" and "honest interior co-bright value ≈ 1.5–1.6" match B2 and the QC verdict.
findings.exact_fix: "...vs 1.0% of papyrus — a 36× over-representation" (and fix the same slip in qc/k3_stage1_review.md B2).

findings.quoted_claim: on a six-pod RTX 5090 fleet (burn $3.49/hr)
findings.artifact_value: $3.49/hr is the *launch* burn (LOG.md line 195: "Burn $3.49/hr; spend at launch $0.62"). The primary QC artifact records a different rate at the time of the stop: qc_live/round1_verdict.md line 39 "Fleet cost note: at ~$4.19/hr" and line 206 "saved ~$4.19/hr". The report's own §4.2 states both correctly ("$19–25 at a $3.49/hr launch burn ($4.19/hr by the time of the stop verdict)"), so §3.6 and §4.2 present different burn rates for the same fleet. Separately, the $4.46 total traces only to LOG.md line 213 — runpod/fleet_stop.py prints `spend ${used:.2f}` from rp.spend() but never persists it, and runpod/balance_baseline.json holds only the $170.3648 baseline. ($4.46 is arithmetically plausible: 6 pods launched ~22:35 per fleet_launch.py mtime, stopped 23:41 per fleet_stop.py mtime ≈ 1.1 h; ($4.46 − $0.62)/1.1 h ≈ $3.5/hr.)
findings.exact_fix: "on a six-pod RTX 5090 fleet ($3.49/hr at launch, $4.19/hr by the stop verdict)". Optionally add to the §3.6 artifact list that the $4.46 figure is recorded in `LOG.md` (RunPod balance delta at termination; not persisted by `runpod/fleet_stop.py`).

findings.quoted_claim: interior-tile Spearman with crack-texture std = **−0.54**
findings.location: sections/03_screens.md §3.10 (and §3.11 item 1: "firing anti-correlates with damage at ρ = −0.54")
findings.artifact_value: −0.54 is ct_std_mat, which salvage/reframe_report.md's own table labels "material texture" (salvage/reframe_interior_check.json ct_std_mat rho = −0.5410). The proxy that reframe_report labels "crack texture" is ct_std_all, whose interior value is −0.5066 ≈ −0.51 (reframe_interior_check.json). The label and the number belong to different columns. The other three §3.10 correlations are exactly right in the interior frame: surf_frac +0.4170 → "+0.42", surf_recovery +0.4125 → "+0.41", meanct_mat +0.6760 → "+0.68"; and the all-tile ρ(meanCT, f05) = 0.7312 → "+0.73" quoted in §3.9/§3.11 is also correct.
findings.exact_fix: "interior-tile Spearman with material-texture std = **−0.54** (crack-texture std −0.51)".

findings.quoted_claim: Nonzero-CT percentiles [p1, p25, p50, p75, p99]: Paris 4 = [26, 49, 91, 116, 158] ... (matching verified: matched p1/p50/p99 = 25/96/154 vs target 26/97/155)
findings.artifact_value: Both are in artifacts, but they are different Paris 4 measurements presented in one paragraph as one reference. [26, 49, 91, 116, 158] is the laptop run (qc_live/round1_verdict.md §5, from qc_indomain_histmatch.py). [26, 97, 155] is tgt_p in qc_live/qc_histmatch_result.json, the pod rerun (qc_histmatch_pod.py). p50 91 vs 97 and p99 158 vs 155 — a referee reading straight through sees Paris 4's median stated as 91 and then matched against a target of 97. The 1203 side is consistent throughout (src_p [16, 47, 196] matches [16, 39, 47, 103, 196] at p1/p50/p99).
findings.exact_fix: Add the provenance: "...(matching verified against the pod-side Paris 4 reference tile, whose p1/p50/p99 = 26/97/155 differ slightly from the laptop tile quoted above: matched p1/p50/p99 = 25/96/154)".

findings.quoted_claim: Under that design, Tack-level ink (84 µg/cm²) becomes a ~5σ event.
findings.artifact_value: The figure is reproducible but only under an assumption the same sentence contradicts. out/k3_sensitivity_bound.json scenarios_raw_frame.Tack_large_84ug gives sigma_d0.5 = 1.01; × the stated 5× σ improvement = 5.05σ — i.e. ~5σ requires KEEPING the d ≈ 0.5 stroke dilution. But upgrade item (i) in the same sentence says the sheet-surface-conformal filter removes "the d ≈ 0.33–0.5 stroke-dilution penalty", which at d = 1 gives sigma_d1.0 = 2.02 × 5 = 10.1σ. The two halves of the recipe cannot both hold. This sentence is report-only — out/k3_sensitivity_bound.md §7 states the ≈5× σ gap and the upgrade list but never converts it to a σ level for Tack ink. (The ≈5× gap itself checks out: 0.12591 / 0.025 = 5.04.)
findings.exact_fix: "Under that design, Tack-level ink (84 µg/cm²) becomes a ~5σ event even if the conformal filter only halves the stroke-dilution penalty, and ~10σ if it removes it."

findings.quoted_claim: the published PHerc.0332 dual-energy null used 53/70 keV, entirely below the edge ... unlike the published PHerc.0332 53/70 keV screen, where Fe (2.03) is degenerate with Pb (2.04) in the same high tail
findings.location: sections/03_screens.md §3, intro paragraph and §3.1 (supporting REPORT.md exec summary bullet 4: "the first screen on this scan pair signed correctly for lead")
findings.artifact_value: The physics is solid and I reproduced it independently from NIST log-log interpolation: Pb 53/70 = 6.9175/3.3951 = 2.0375 → "2.04" (json ratios.Pb_53_70); Fe 53 keV = 1.677, Fe 70 keV = 0.826 → 2.030 → "2.03"; Pb 74/110 = 2.9484/4.3727 = 0.6743 → "0.674"; Ca ≈ 1.4 and Fe = 2.25 at 74/110 are in qc/k3_stage1_review.md's physics table (I get Fe = 2.252). The gap is bibliographic: the prior work the whole novelty framing rests on is never named or cited in §3 — no author, no link, no date, twice. It is named only in out/k3_sensitivity_bound.md §5 ("axiosdevs, 53/70 keV"), and even there without a reference, while Tack and Brun get full DOIs and PMC links. The memo also carries a hedge §3 omits: "we do not have axiosdevs' σ, thresholds, or window parameters and make no quantitative claim about their sensitivity." And no artifact anywhere records a prior-work search for the Paris 4 74/110 pair, so REPORT.md's "first screen on this scan pair signed correctly for lead" is an unrecorded literature-negative.
findings.exact_fix: In §3.1, name and link the prior work on first mention: "...unlike the published PHerc.0332 53/70 keV screen (axiosdevs, [link/date]), where Fe (2.03) is degenerate with Pb (2.04) in the same high tail. We do not have that screen's σ, thresholds or window parameters, so we make no quantitative comparison of sensitivity — the contrast here is structural, in the energy pair." And soften the exec-summary claim to "the first screen we are aware of on this scan pair signed correctly for lead" unless a literature search is recorded.

sections.coverage_note:
WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. (1) I did not re-run the stage-2 screen end to end — the LOW/HIGH channel voxel counts (2 and 51,343) are taken from out/k3_s2_stats.json as produced. I verified the pipeline logic by reading k3_stage2_screen.py line by line and reproduced its calibration constants exactly from the L1 arrays (air offsets and both p75 gates matched to full float precision), which is strong evidence the recorded run is faithful, but the channel counts themselves are single-run outputs with no independent replicate. (2) The 30,258 cluster count and the $4.46 spend are structurally unverifiable — neither the labelled mask nor the RunPod balance delta was persisted. (3) My n_tested re-derivation (2.63e8) extrapolates 464 sampled slices to 2,033; the co-bright fraction (20.3%, per-slab 18.2–25.4%) is a within-voxel ratio and is robust to that extrapolation, but the absolute n carries a few percent of sampling error. (4) I did not verify the L0 human-verification verdicts in the §3.4 cluster table ("nodular incrustation" / "PSF-mismatch artifact") — sizes and centroids match out/k3_s2_high_clusters.json exactly, but the verdict column rests on visual review recorded only in the figure out/k3_s2_high_verify.png, which I did not open. (5) I did not re-derive the NIST mass-attenuation values from XCOM; I log-log interpolated from memory of the NIST tables and got Pb 74 keV = 2.948 (json 2.9484), Pb 110 keV = 4.318 (json 4.3727, 1.3% apart), Fe 74/110 = 2.252, Fe 53/70 = 2.030 — good enough to confirm signs and one significant figure, not to certify the third digit. The memo's own caveat ("re-verify against XCOM before external publication") still stands. (6) I did not check the figures (k3_s2_high_verify.png, k3_psfmatch2.png, morph_gallery.png, atlas_1203.png) against their captions.

WHAT IS CLEAN, after opening the artifacts. §3.2 (method): every parameter reproduces from k3_stage2_screen.py — 3-voxel erosion, den≥14 aggregation, 32-slice sub-block radial detrend, 4σ threshold, σ = 0.12591, p75 gates 0.1171/0.0998, offsets −0.0310/−0.0268, HALO=2 ("2-slice halo" is right; the script's own docstring saying "1-slice" is wrong). §3.3 sensitivity block: every figure matches out/k3_sensitivity_bound.json — 311 µg/cm² saturation, 576 µg/cm² re-cross, 639 µg/cm² both-clip, 0.270/0.200 = 1.35 plateau, 1.1–1.7σ at d = 0.33–0.5, 203–343 µg/cm² 3σ window at ≥88% coverage, and 203.2/84 = 2.42 and 203.2/16 = 12.7 → "2.4× and 13×" both recompute. The "no saturation channel was implemented" statement is a REAL code gap, not a hedge: k3_stage2_screen.py contains no u8 == 255 test anywhere, the mask is `(u74>0)&(u110>0)` with no upper bound, and to_float() maps clipped values linearly with no flag. §3.4's 28-window null reproduces exactly from comb/comb_skeptic_k3.json (span 1.17–1.52, IQR 1.26–1.38, 5/28 ≥ 1.43, two same-ring windows at 1.5235/1.5238 above both flagged values 1.4813/1.4648) — only the "~p80" gloss is off. The √λ PSF argument checks: √(110/74) = 1.2192 → "~22% more blurred". §3.1's stage-1 statistics all reproduce from out/k3_stage1_stats.json. Part B: I loaded all three frozen-benchmark files and they are readable and self-consistent — tiles.parquet 496,786×14 with exactly 29,748 scored rows across the 14 listed z-slabs, proxies.parquet 29,748×25, atlas_1203.npy (60,104,104) float32 with exactly 29,748 finite cells spread over exactly 14 z-planes, plus a genuinely good atlas_1203_README.md; f05 min = 0.00176 confirms 0 silent tiles directly from the data, and median 0.0645 confirms "5–7% of voxels". The scorecard numbers all trace: background f05 0.0007 and edge band 0.1386→0.139 recomputed from qc_morph_result.json aggregate; p5–p95 0.01819–0.09593 from qc_stats_result.json (n_run 3346); 94.5–98.8% agreement and r 0.637–0.753 from qc_norm_equiv_result.json (note the report's "r = 0.64–0.75" uses the core-region correlations; the full-tile values are 0.617–0.705, unstated but defensible). The anti-clustering retirement in §3.7 is exact (NN 2.132 vs 3.139±0.083, z = −12.1; 0.00–0.45 over 50 thinnings). All of §3.9's regression and geography statistics match salvage/scalar_report.md, and all of §3.10's dominance results match salvage/reframe_report.md and reframe_correlations.json (AUC 0.892 vs 0.855, partial ρ −0.001 vs block null −0.012±0.010, ΔR² 0.0000). The morphology census figures in §3.8 all match salvage/morph_report.md. The two apparently-conflicting tile counts are reconcilable, not a contradiction: morph_report's "35,148 scored tiles" is the raw scored-row count and 29,748 is the count after deduplicating 5,400 double-scored tiles, as scalar_report §1 documents.

findings.quoted_claim: **The empty-volume QC gate** (`hunt/check_air.py`): sample a mesh's vertices against the masked volume at pyramid level 3 and reject any segment with a material fraction reading zero. Seconds per segment, no GPU. It flags 18 of 66 published GP surfaces
findings.artifact_value: hunt/check_air.py wrote hunt/out/vertex_material.json — 10 rows, not 66. The '18 of 66' figure comes from a different, cheaper measurement: hunt/out/corpus_oob.json (77 rows; 26 with frac_out_of_array > 0 → 18 unique meshes, all PHerc1447), a pure array-bounds comparison that reads no volume, per hunt/geometry_compare.md §7.1(a). That doc explicitly calls the bounds check 'a strict lower bound on the defect — it misses every vertex that is inside the array but in masked/unscanned space, which is the larger population'. The level-3 material-fraction measurement described in the report ran on 11 targeted segments (hunt/out/corpus_material.json), finding 7 of 9 PHerc1447 meshes with 27–96% of vertices on zero-valued voxels. The PHerc0813 half of the claim is sound (hunt/pherc0813_mesh_qc.json: auto_grown_20260818043513298, surface_zero_frac 1.0, mean 0.0 DN).
findings.exact_fix: **The empty-volume QC gate** (`hunt/check_air.py`, `hunt/corpus_material.py`): sample a mesh's vertices against the masked volume at pyramid level 3 and reject any segment with a material fraction reading zero; the free bounds-only variant needs no volume read at all. The bounds check flags 18 of 66 published GP surfaces, all PHerc1447 (`hunt/out/corpus_oob.json`), and level-3 sampling on nine of the worst finds seven with 27–96% of their vertices on empty voxels (`hunt/out/corpus_material.json`) — a strict lower bound either way. It caught the same defect immediately on our own newly grown PHerc0813 patches (§2.9).

findings.quoted_claim: Every result-producing run in Track D was followed by an adversarial audit — a separate pass (in practice, a separate agent session with no stake in the result) whose protocol was fixed

'Every' is also not literally true: the K2b 14-scroll index was verified by a self-run recompute (report/scripts/verify_index_air_refs.py, §1 line 25), and LOG.md 2026-08-17 records that the report's own line-by-line fact-check and prize-fit review 'died on the monthly spend limit' and were replaced by a self-run script.
findings.exact_fix: Add as the last sentence of §4.1: 'One limitation belongs here and not only in the limitations list: these were separate sessions, not separate people or separate codebases — the same agent framework produced the results and attacked them, and a small number of checks (the 14-scroll index recompute, this report's own numeric verification) are self-runs rather than adversarial passes. What substitutes for independence is the discipline itself: exact reproduction before interpretation, matched nulls, a named mundane explanation, and every number landed in a shipped JSON a reader can recompute (limitation 12).'

WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK. (1) Process claims with no artifact: "K1's kill rule (|AUC−0.5| < 0.02) was fixed before the data was fetched" — LOG.md day 1 asserts pre-registration but there is no timestamped pre-registration file; same for "the K1b depth-contrast statistic was frozen before touching the held-out segments" (this one is circumstantially supported: qc/k1_k2_review.md B1/W4 demanded the freeze at 16:36 and out/k1b_depth_validation.json was written at 19:31) and for row 11's "a verification step that was committed to before the screen ran" (LOG.md records the verification agent launching only after the flag appeared; the FLAG_VERDICT protocol itself is post-hoc, though the four prescriptions were then pre-registered for v2). (2) Cross-section claims restated in §4 that belong to §1-§3 and that I spot-checked only: the 2-5 ROIs/scroll gate, the "only GP-eligible data above the resolution wall", the §2.5/§2.8 four-test battery contents, the §3.7 scorecard numbers. (3) I did not re-run any GPU/pod work, did not touch RunPod, and did not verify the fleet cost figures beyond LOG.md (the $4.46/$80/$3.49-hr/$4.19-hr/$0.62/$0.40/$70-guard/169k-tiles/5.5h/1.5-2.7 tiles-s/73%-skip/6-pod numbers all trace to LOG.md 2026-08-16 cloud phase and 2026-08-17 early AM plus qc_live/round1_verdict.md, but there is no billing export in the repo to audit them against — $4.46 is a point-in-time figure and is correctly hedged as such, since LOG.md later records $5.61 then $33.38 account-wide).

WHAT I VERIFIED CLEAN (opened the artifact, recomputed where arithmetic was involved). Ledger rows 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12 all trace to a real audit document that says what the row says, with every quoted number matching. Specifically: row 2's w039 0.513 / w040 0.501 / w041 0.466-inverted / held-out mean 0.4934 (recomputed 0.49337 from out/k1b_depth_validation.json); row 5's 0.651/0.917 → 0.427 and 100.0% no-data background; row 6's 0.614/0.902, z = 5.82, 72% off-sheet, 0.5035 at z = 0.34 with 18/40 nulls above, 12-29% of nulls faking the profile, (−36,+39) px misregistration; row 7's >5σ→~1.0σ/~0.3σ and "6 arithmetic/model errors" (the referee notes list 7 fixes, item 7 self-labelled cosmetic — 6 is the defensible count); row 9's p = 0.97 and 74.7/77.5/77.3 DN; row 10's 79% / 25-40 µm / 0.2% / 17.5° vs 50-60°; row 11's 3.92 vs 8.43 (ratio 2.15 → "2.2×"), +0.54 / p = 0.18 / 71-of-400, E[#z≥5] = 1.07 vs 1, lowest Fourier bin, ρ(1P) = −0.269, 90.8% halo, 64-px lattice; row 12's z = +13.74, ρ = +0.370 across 69, 0-of-71 vs control 5-of-5, +25.6 → +16.3 (and I recomputed the two separation ratios myself: 13.74/5.94 = 2.31 → "2.3×", 16.3/4.64 = 3.51 → "3.5×", neither of which appears as a stored number in PROTOCOL_V2.md). §4.1's five reproductions all check (K1 max delta 1.9×10⁻⁴; K3 "reproduces every JSON value"; S1a v1 "exactly"; S1a v2 "every per-tile AUC at every k to 4 decimals"; fleet f05 0.06952 and 0.03924 on both machines = 5 dp). §4.1's ESS block recomputes exactly from qc/qc_s1a_v2_nulls.json: n_pos = 40,093 ("n ≈ 40,000"), naive sd 0.00251, block sd 0.0303, (0.0303/0.00251)² = 145.7 → 146.3 stored, 40,093/146.3 = 274.0 → "roughly 275". §4.5 checks throughout: 9.5/10.0/23.3×, 2.6-3.8 DN vs 0.289 DN = 9.0-13.1×, the three air-referenced crossings (q = 0.433/0.444/0.499 → 9.362/(2q) = 10.81/10.54/9.38 µm), 7-39×, ~25× site spread (24.6×), and the degraded-tier claim recomputed from out/k2b_index/: five scrolls at SNR 8.45-24.35 ("8.5-24.4") with the next scroll at 72.20, gap 2.97× ("3.0×", generous but inside rounding). §4.2's five-of-eight-silent vs 0-of-3,346, the doubled firing under histogram matching (0.0392 → 0.0810), ~45% completion, 29,748 tiles, and 2.403 µm (meta/PHerc1203.json pixel_size_um) all check. §4.6's gates check: ~5 min/segment is right (survey_all.json mean 285.1 s = 4.75 min/segment, median 3.4 min), the corpus tripwire really is 0 hits over 80 segments × 2 directions = 160 inferences with 0 errors, the ink_9um null blocks really are 256 full-res px (salvage/verdict_periodicity.py), the comb 28-window base rates (1.17-1.52, IQR 1.26-1.38) and the 60%→97.3% matched baseline are verbatim in comb/COMB_VERDICT.md, and every script path named in §4.6 items 1-8 exists on disk. §4.3's "five of the twelve entries (1, 5, 6, and partially 3, 9)" is self-consistent — the enumeration is five and each of the five is a defensible instance of the named trap, though rows 8 and 11 (a partial sample that isn't the population; a 16-draw null that isn't the null) fit the trap at least as well as row 9 does and are not counted.

TOOL-COVERAGE GAP WORTH KNOWING. report/scripts/verify_report.py still passes (11 checks, 0 problems, re-run just now) but its coverage of §4 is almost nil: it checks the K1b four segments plus held-out mean, and nothing else in this section. It does not check the ledger row count, the six-item claim, the 72-hour claim, the $4.46, the tripwire pre-registration, the "deleted" k2_spectra keys, the 18-of-66 attribution, the −12.6, or the five-test naming — i.e. every finding above sits outside the verifier's reach. If any of these fixes land, consider adding a §4 block to that script (row count, an assertion that out/k2_spectra.json does not contain smallest_recoverable_halfperiod_um, and a corpus_oob-vs-vertex_material row-count check would cover three of them cheaply).

1. Whether the promised repo would actually publish cleanly. That is large for GitHub but under any hard limit; no single file exceeds 50 MB.

2. Runtime claims. I did not execute anything expensive: not k2b_detectability_index.py, not analyze_survey_corpus_v2.py, not any renderer or inference path, and nothing that streams S3 in bulk. I ran only report/scripts/verify_report.py (0 problems, 11 checks) and report/scripts/corpus_summary.py (clean, wrote corpus_summary.json). So sec E's time estimates ("CPU, ~1 h", "CPU, hours (resumable)", "1 pod, ~2 h", "6-pod fleet, ~5.5 h") are UNVERIFIED, as is COMMUNITY_POST's "runs in seconds at pyramid level 3" for hunt/check_air.py - hunt/out/check_air.log is 0 bytes, so no timing evidence exists on disk for that claim either.

3. Entry-point verification was partial, as scoped. I inspected argparse/argv handling for 7 scripts (render_tifxyz_sv.py: full argparse, 3 positionals + 8 options; survey_segments.py: documented `python survey_segments.py <shard_id> <n_shards>`, matches sys.argv[1:3]; analyze_survey_corpus_v2.py: argparse --nperm/--jobs/--only/--out/--figure-only; corpus_summary.py: no args, ran clean; check_air.py: NO argparse, reads hunt/meshcache/segs.json positionally-free; verify_index_air_refs.py and k2b_detectability_index.py: no args, constants at top). 4. Licensing is a factual not a legal check. I verified no weights and no bulk scroll data are currently inside trackD, and that no LICENSE exists. I did NOT re-verify the current text of the Vesuvius Challenge data agreement at scrollprize.org/data - the report's own [BEN] bracket in sec G already flags that the CC BY-NC characterization comes from the acceptance flow rather than a legal reading, and I am not the right check for that.

Deliberately out of my lane, flagged for the section reviewers rather than adjudicated: whether "66 unique surfaces" is the right denominator for "23 z_dbg dumps" (23 is a count of catalogue ROWS; only 22 z_dbg base names are distinct, and the 66 figure derives from a geometry de-duplication I did not reproduce); whether the v2 screen should have scored 80 rather than 75 segments given the 10 recovered maps; and every physics/statistics claim in sections 1-4 beyond the specific numbers I recomputed as cross-checks on COMMUNITY_POST.

judges.lens: Hostile methodological referee of the ScrollPrize #191 school — I attack the strongest claims, not the weakest, and I care only whether they survive contact with the repo the author himself is shipping. I opened the primary artifacts rather than reading the prose, and I recomputed the three measurements that decide whether the headline results stand.
judges.verdict:
As of right now this is not a submission — it is a manuscript. No git repo anywhere under C:\Users\benbl\Desktop\Vsuvious\trackD, no LICENSE, no README, no public URL, and 36 unfilled [BEN:] placeholders including the title, the framing paragraph, the AI-assistance disclosure and every closing. Progress prizes require an open-source release; without one the band is no_award regardless of content. Treat everything below as a judgement on the delivered version Ben will actually produce.

On content: this is a genuinely disciplined measurement-and-methods submission with no unlock. Its differentiation is rigor, and a pitch built entirely on rigor has no floor — if rigor is punctured there is no fallback claim. I punctured it three times in about forty minutes, using only files the repo itself ships.

(1) The positive control is on training data and the report never says so. trackD/meta/ink9um_corpus.md is titled "ink_9um labeled training corpus" and lists w035 in BOTH training manifests (aligned-scrollprizeorg-21slices, native9-scrollprizeorg-21slices), and states that validation masks exist for exactly three segments — pherc0139-w016, pherc0814-46527, pherc1667-w029 — of which w035 is not one. So "pixel AUC 0.9991/0.9982" is an on-training-data score. The labels are human so it is not circular in the label sense, and the number is real, but the phrase "validated instrument" is doing work it has not earned. The word "training" appears exactly once in the entire report — in a figure caption at 02_instrument.md:272 — and never in §2.2, §2.4, §2.7, the executive summary, or COMMUNITY_POST.md. A referee greps one file and the framing flips from "validated instrument found nothing" to "instrument we never independently validated found nothing on surfaces nobody expected text on."

(2) The screen fails on the ground truth itself, and the report claims the opposite. out/survey/corpus_analysis_v2.json control record w035_LABELS — the human ink labels, run through the identical v2 protocol — returns z = +0.256, empirical p = 0.328, 3 gates of 5. FAIL. The project's own out/survey/PROTOCOL_V2.md lines 371-377 says it in bold: "A handful of letters on an otherwise blank sheet would not trip this screen." Meanwhile 02_instrument.md §2.7's bounded claim asserts the instrument "would have flagged ~5 mm-ruled text," and REPORT.md line 40 headlines the screen. PROTOCOL_V2.md is linked from the report as the protocol document. The control passes only because the model's dense page-wide response field carries the ruling; the letters alone do not. That is a page-scale test of a response field, not a letter-scale test of text, and the report has the measurement and omits it.

(3) The index's read anchor inverts under a like-for-like reference. I re-ran k2b_detectability_index.validate_air on D:\vesuvius-data\trackD\qc_roi_PHerc0139_air2_128.npy (the K2 audit's clean 128³ window, recorded in qc/qc_k2_air0139.json): it PASSES the index's own gates — mean 50.0 DN vs gate 63.0, flatness 24.56 vs gate 40. §1.1 asserts "PHerc0139 produced no genuine air window anywhere (all candidates rejected by the gates)." False; one exists in the project's own cache and passes. Feeding it as the noise reference to the index's own three PHerc0139 papyrus ROIs gives SNR@0.25 = 17.08 / 20.63 / 22.23, median 20.63 — against the shipped 115.54. That places the read anchor at rank 12 of 14, inside the degraded tier, BELOW PHerc1218 (24.35), PHerc0268 (23.60) and PHerc0257 (22.71). §1.5's central claim — "the five degraded-tier scrolls measurably do not reach that class" — is then false, and with it the report's single most actionable recommendation ("the bottom five are where a model failure cannot be blamed on the model"). The "conservative 39×" the report leans on is the audit's DIFFERENT papyrus site, not a site-matched measurement.

Add the arithmetic own-goals in the document whose pitch is arithmetic: REPORT.md says the corrections ledger has "Twelve" (line 27), "ten" (line 48) and "eleven-row" (line 59) — three counts of one 12-row table in one file. "72 hours" is ~50 (earliest artifact 2026-08-16 15:51, latest 2026-08-18 18:31). The "3.0× gap" is 2.9651, and the report's own verify_report.py prints 2.97 while asserting only a 2.9–3.1 band. "66 unique surfaces" is contradicted by report/scripts/corpus_summary.py — the script the report advertises as recomputing every §2 corpus number — which emits 65.

None of this makes the work bad. The work is better than most of what wins $1K. But the delivery currently hands a hostile reader the exact weapon the report claims immunity to.
judges.strongest_element:
The forward/reverse render-symmetry discriminator — and it is stronger than the report knows, because I just measured the control it is missing.

The logic is clean and needs no periodicity machinery, no permutation nulls, and no assumption about hand, ruling or language: ink sits on one face of a sheet, so reversing the render's z-order should destroy the map. Control 0.055–0.094; corpus minimum 0.222 over 80 independent surfaces, median 0.637. That is a bimodal separation with no overlap across three scrolls and 160 inferences, and gate_fwd_rev alone kills 71 of 71.

The obvious hostile attack is that it is a pipeline confound: analyze_survey_corpus_v2.py lines 71-73 point the control at out/ink9um_w035/w035_seed42-075000.tif, which per §2.2 is the prediction on the PUBLISHED 28-slice surface volume, while all 71 corpus segments are custom 21-slice renders from runpod/render_tifxyz_sv.py. Different renderer, different slice count, different provenance — so "control asymmetric, corpus symmetric" could be a renderer artifact rather than an ink signal, and that would take down the decisive gate and with it the headline.

The refuting measurement takes thirty seconds and the two TIFFs have been sitting on disk since 2026-08-17 11:03. I computed it:
  published surface volume, fwd vs rev, either-nonzero support: r = 0.09426 (n = 27,169,536)
  custom tifxyz render,     fwd vs rev, either-nonzero support: r = 0.09394 (n = 26,914,112)
Identical to three decimals. The renderer preserves the control's z-asymmetry exactly. The gate is measuring the sheet, not the pipeline.

That single number closes the strongest structural objection to the report's headline result, and it is nowhere in the report, in salvage/verdict_consistency.json, or in any JSON in the tree. Ship it.

Second-strongest, and the most adoptable thing here: runpod/render_tifxyz_sv.py. All 14 released ink_9um checkpoints embed mode:"flat" and the native-3D path hard-refuses them, so the released checkpoints are unrunnable on any scroll without a published surface volume. This renderer unlocks them, end-to-end validated at r = 0.813 (I reproduced 0.8133 from the two TIFFs). That is a concrete capability the community does not currently have, and it is worth more to a judge than the null.

The positive control. Everything in §2 hangs from one segment, and that segment has three independent problems the report does not state.

n = 1. out/k1b_depth_validation.json shows w039 (182,426 ink px), w040 (716,497) and w041 (229,883) were already fetched, with human labels and published surface volumes, and used in K1b. None was ever run through ink_9um or the corpus screen. There is no ink9um_w039/ directory anywhere in out/. Training-set membership, undisclosed (see verdict).

The screen fails on that control's own ground-truth labels: z = +0.26, p = 0.33, 3/5 gates. So the instrument's demonstrated sensitivity is to a dense page-wide model response, not to text. Every sentence of the form "an instrument that reads human-verified letters at AUC 0.999 and would have flagged ~5 mm-ruled text" (02_instrument.md §2.7, REPORT.md line 21) is stronger than the artifacts support.

Downstream, this is what makes the corpus null thin. A hostile reader lines up: the sample is 23 of 66 tracker debug dumps, 18 of 66 partly outside the reconstructed volume, index ranks 8/13/14 with only one readable-tier scroll — the report says all of this itself, admirably — screened by an instrument validated once, on training data, that cannot detect sparse letters. The honest information content of "0 of 71" is then close to zero, because nobody ever claimed those surfaces bore text and the instrument was never shown able to find text on a surface that has some but is not saturated with it.
judges.what_a_hostile_reviewer_attacks_first:
`grep -i w035 trackD/meta/ink9um_corpus.md`. That is the whole attack, and the file ships with the repo by the report's own artifact list.

It lands first because it is one command, it hits the strongest claim rather than the weakest, and it is asymmetric: it does not require the reviewer to dispute a single number. Every number in §2.2 is correct. The AUC is real, the labels are human, the reproduction is genuine. What collapses is the word "validated," and that word is load-bearing for all five deliverables — deliverable 2 is literally titled "A validated cross-scroll ink instrument."

The second move is worse, because it is the report's own document turning on it: open out/survey/PROTOCOL_V2.md — linked from REPORT.md line 103 as the protocol of record — and read line 375 in bold. "A handful of letters on an otherwise blank sheet would not trip this screen." Then read 02_instrument.md §2.7: the instrument "would have flagged ~5 mm-ruled text." A reviewer who finds the report and its own linked protocol contradicting each other on the sensitivity of the headline screen stops extending good faith, and after that every remaining caveat reads as damage control rather than as disclosure.

The third move is cheap and cosmetic and does disproportionate harm because of what this report claims to be: count the ledger. §4.3 has 12 rows. REPORT.md says twelve, ten, and eleven-row, in one file. A referee will quote those three phrases side by side in a Discord thread and that quotation, not the corpus screen, becomes what people remember. "72 hours" is ~50h by mtime. "3.0×" is 2.9651 and the shipped verifier prints 2.97. "66 unique surfaces" is 65 per the report's own corpus_summary.py.

Fourth, if the reviewer is a scan-quality person: the §1 anchor. qc/qc_k2_air0139.json ships, §1.2 note (a) points a reader straight at it, and re-referencing takes one call to the project's own validate_air. 20.63, not 115.54, rank 12 of 14.

Note what is NOT on this list. Nobody will attack the corpus null for being a null. This community publishes negatives and retracts headlines in days; a clean negative with a matched null is respected. What gets attacked is a rigor claim that the shipped artifacts do not support.
