This also gives r = 0.813 a primary artifact, which REPRODUCIBILITY.md's preamble currently promises for every headline number and does not deliver.

STATE THE LABELS-ONLY CONTROL AND FIX THE SENSITIVITY CLAIM. Add to §2.4 right after the gate cascade: 'One bound on this screen, measured rather than assumed: run on w035''s human ink labels themselves — 13 letter components on a 54 mm profile — the identical protocol returns z = +0.26, p = 0.328, 3 gates of 5 (out/survey/corpus_analysis_v2.json, control record w035_LABELS). It is a page-scale test of the model''s response field, not a letter-scale test. Sparse text on an otherwise blank sheet would not trip it; that regime is covered by the tripwire and the morphology battery, both also clean.' Then replace §2.7's 'would have flagged ~5 mm-ruled text' with 'would have flagged a page-scale ~5 mm ruling.' This converts a claim your own linked PROTOCOL_V2.md refutes into a self-bound, which is the thing the report is selling.

PROMOTE YOUR BEST RESULT OUT OF hunt/geometry_compare.md, WHERE IT IS BURIED. Lines 36-41 document PHerc1447 auto_grown_20250702235910292: lamella modulation 0.370 against the control's 0.357, interface sharpness 0.101 vs 0.078, 18 of 18 tiles with a resolvable lamella, 0 % empty volume — it matches the control on every statistic that separates the control from the corpus — and it produced the LOWEST forward/reverse correlation in the entire 80-segment corpus (r = 0.222) and still no letters, no tripwire hit. That is the fair single test the report keeps saying it does not have, and it defeats the report's own leading alternative explanation (lamella contrast) on the one segment where that explanation cannot apply. Right now REPORT.md line 43 says 'only PHerc1203 was a fair test' and §2.7 says the same, so the report is arguing against its own strongest evidence. Give this segment a named paragraph in §2.7 and a clause in the executive summary. It is worth more than the aggregate 0-of-71.

FIX THE PHerc0139 ANCHOR, which currently inverts. §1.1's 'PHerc0139 produced no genuine air window anywhere (all candidates rejected by the gates)' is false: D:\vesuvius-data\trackD\qc_roi_PHerc0139_air2_128.npy passes your own validate_air (mean 50.0 DN vs gate 63.0, flatness 24.56 vs gate 40). Re-referencing the index's own three PHerc0139 ROIs against it gives SNR@0.25 = 17.08 / 20.63 / 22.23, median 20.63 — rank 12 of 14, inside the degraded tier, below PHerc1218 (24.35), PHerc0268 (23.60) and PHerc0257 (22.71). So §1.5's 'the five degraded-tier scrolls measurably do not reach that class' is not supported, and the '39×' floor is a different papyrus site, not a site-matched value. Rewrite §1.5 around what survives: the readable tier exceeds every measured PHerc0139 site (17.1–38.6 on a common air reference) by ≥ 1.9×, and the degraded tier does not separate from the calibrator, so no claim about the degraded tier can be anchored on 0139. Publish the site-matched number in note (a) — disclosing that your own anchor lands mid-table is exactly the move that makes the rigor pitch credible.

TAKE THE POSITIVE CONTROL FROM n = 1 TO n = 4. w039, w040 and w041 have human ink labels and published native-9 µm surface volumes, were already fetched for K1b (out/k1b_depth_validation.json: 182,426 / 716,497 / 229,883 ink px), and were never run through ink_9um. Running seed42 forward and reverse on all three and putting them through the v2 protocol costs roughly the same as the $1.15 already spent on the instrument. Even though they are also in the training manifest, four controls passing 5/5 while 71 segments pass 0/5 is a categorically stronger discrimination claim than one control, and it directly answers 'your gates are calibrated on a single example.' If you want a genuinely held-out control, meta/ink9um_corpus.md names the three the released checkpoints actually validate on — pherc0139-w016, pherc0814-46527, pherc1667-w029 — none at native 9 µm, which is itself a finding worth one sentence.

RENDER AND INFER THE FIVE ON-MATERIAL PHerc0813 PATCHES (~$0.70, already scoped in the §2.9 [BEN:] note). This is the only path to a positive result in this cycle, and it converts §2.9 from 'we grew geometry that may not track lamellae' into an actual first: the first ink inference ever run on PHerc0813. Even a null there is worth more than the corpus null, because PHerc0813 is index rank 1 and same-campaign as the calibrator, so it is the first fair scan-quality test the project would have. Report it either way, including the honest reading if the 0.036–0.074 modulation predicts what it looks like it predicts.

CUT THE REPORT BY HALF AND LEAD WITH THE TOOLS. 1,153 lines across six files is more than any judge reads, and the current lead — a corpus-wide null over a sample you yourself describe as debug dumps and out-of-volume meshes — is the weakest thing in the package. Lead instead with: (a) the scan-quality index for 14 GP volumes, (b) the renderer that makes flat-mode ink_9um checkpoints runnable on any 9 µm segment, (c) the forward/reverse asymmetry statistic as a free, checkpoint-agnostic ink discriminator with the cross-render control attached, (d) the first geometry on PHerc0813, (e) the pre-fleet acceptance gate that stopped a fleet at $4.46. The corpus null is the evidence those tools work, not the headline. 'Measure before you hunt' is a good thesis; make the measuring instruments the deliverable.

FIX THE ARITHMETIC IN THE DOCUMENT THAT SELLS ARITHMETIC, and extend verify_report.py to cover it. REPORT.md says the ledger has 'Twelve' (line 27), 'ten' (line 48) and 'eleven-row' (line 59) — §4.3 has 12 rows. '72 hours' is ~50 h (earliest artifact 2026-08-16 15:51 to latest 2026-08-18 18:31). '3.0× gap' is 2.9651 and your own verify_report.py prints 2.97 while asserting only 2.9 < gap < 3.1. '66 unique surfaces' is 65 by report/scripts/corpus_summary.py, the script REPORT.md line 104 advertises as recomputing every §2 corpus number; §2.4's PHerc1447 cell of 38 matches neither 37 (name) nor 41 (SHA-1). REPRODUCIBILITY.md §E still totals $5.61 'entire project' against the executive summary's ~$11 and has no corpus-survey line at all. §4.3 row 3 says two k2_spectra.json keys were 'deleted' — they are still in the file. Then add assertions for the ledger row count, the tier gap exact value, the unique-surface count and the k2_spectra keys to verify_report.py, because every one of these findings sits outside its current 11 checks.

judges.lens: Vesuvius Challenge Progress Prize judge allocating a fixed monthly pot, calibrating against Jul 2026 ($20K ScrollFiesta auto-meshing; $10K-tier annotation tooling and Khartes3D; $2.5K patch-aggregation failure-mode notebooks; $1K each for zarr read fixes, an ink-detection validation harness, self-intersection detection, spiral fitting). The operative question is not "is this rigorous" — it plainly is — but "whose next month changes because this exists, and is the author visibly a human pursuing the project's goals."
judges.verdict:
It wins something. It does not win the month, and it is not close to the $10-20K tier. Calibrate honestly: in July 2026 an *ink-detection validation harness* — the closest artifact in the historical record to this report's most reusable output — was priced at $1K. Failure-mode analysis notebooks priced at $2.5K. The $10K/$20K tier went exclusively to things that made the pipeline produce more: auto-meshing, annotation tooling that halved a human's time, Khartes3D. Nothing in this report makes the pipeline produce one more mesh, one more label, or one more read letter. It measures. Measurement of this quality has an observed market price in this competition and it is $1K-$2.5K.

I land it at $2.5K as the realistic outcome, and I want to be precise about the distribution around that, because it is wide and Ben controls most of it:

DOWNSIDE, and it is live right now: there is no git repository anywhere in the tree, no LICENSE, no README, no public URL. Ben's own BEN_TODO A6 calls this a hard eligibility requirement. Separately, every [BEN:] block is unfilled — title, framing, AI-assistance disclosure, four per-section motivation sentences, two closing claims, the closing paragraph. Submitted in that state to a team whose CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly closes LLM "fishing expedition" contributions and demands human-written commentary, this reads as an agent artifact with the author's name on the form. That is no_award or a courtesy $500-$1K, and it would have nothing to do with the quality of the work.

UPSIDE to $5K, and it is genuinely reachable in the thirteen days remaining: public repo with the four reuse tools packaged and one-command runnable; every [BEN:] block written in Ben's voice; the three COMMUNITY_POST drafts actually posted with a week to accumulate replies; the k2c separability axis and the ROI-picker correction folded into §1. That last one is the difference between "an index" and "an index, plus the discovery that my own index was measuring the wrong material, plus the corrected axis" — which is a materially better story and it is already computed and sitting on disk.

The structural problem no editing fixes: the five deliverables never close a loop. The index ranks scrolls by scan quality. The corpus screen ran on the only three scrolls with published segments — which the index ranks 8, 13 and 14 of 14. The forward answer to that gap (grow surfaces on rank 1, PHerc0813) produced eight patches that the author's own later measurement puts at 67.3° to the local sheet normal, 0 of 8 within 30°, i.e. unusable. So no deliverable ever pointed the validated instrument at a readable-tier scroll's real surface. The instrument works, the screen is exhaustive, the negative is honest — and the one experiment that would have made it a finding rather than a survey is the one that did not land.

On B3 (one entry vs split): one entry, but that is not the real question. The real question is packaging. As a single 1,150-line document across seven files, a judge reads the exec summary and the limitations and forms an impression of a large careful negative — $2.5K. As one entry that hands over four separately-consumable, separately-announced tools (the tifxyz→surface-volume renderer, the ≤30-tile pre-fleet gate, the ~5min/segment text battery + tripwire, the frozen ink_3d benchmark), each with its own README and invocation, the judge sees things to pick up on Monday. Same content, different band.

On the Limitations: ten of the twelve read as integrity and are the best-written prose in the document. Two are the author talking himself out of money. Limitation 1 ("No ink was found, anywhere, by anything, in this work") is not a limitation, it is the result — leading the list with it invites a judge to score the absence rather than the instrument. And the §2.7 scope bound is stated four separate times (exec summary, five-minute table, Limitation 2, §2.7 itself). Once is credibility; four times is apology, and it trains the reader to discount the screen before they have finished the summary.
judges.strongest_element: The self-correction round trip in §2.4/§2.6, and it is not close. One segment of 80 cleared the first pass's threshold at z=+5.94. Rather than caveating it, a dedicated 400-permutation verification killed it (+0.54, p=0.18), and then — instead of stopping there — the entire corpus was re-scored under a hardened protocol that also cut the author's own positive control from z=+25.6 to +16.3. Correcting your control in the direction that costs you margin, and publishing that the first pass's ordering was substantially permutation noise (Spearman ρ=+0.37, four of five top hits collapsed), is the single most credible act in the document. It leaves a real discrimination margin behind it: the human-verified control passes 5 of 5 gates at z=+16.3 with 0 of 200 shuffles beating it, while 0 of 71 corpus segments pass, the tightest gate (fwd/rev symmetry) failing 71/71. That is a working instrument with a measured separation, not a story about one. A close second, and the thing a judge would most plausibly *use* next month, is the tifxyz→surface-volume renderer: all 14 released ink_9um checkpoints embed mode:"flat" and the native-3D path hard-refuses them, so render-then-infer is the only runnable route on any scroll without a published surface volume. That is a real hole in community tooling and this fills it — but it is buried as bullet 4 of 10 in the artifact list and its r=0.813 validation exists only in prose, in a report that promises every headline number lands in a JSON.
judges.weakest_element: §1, the scan-quality index — which is the deliverable the report leads with, and the one the title is built around. Three compounding problems. (a) The author's own later work, computed 2026-08-18 17:20-18:42 and sitting in out/k2c_separability/k2c_analysis.json, shows the index's ROI picker scores candidates by highest smoothed intensity and therefore selects the brightest dense material in each scroll — mineral incrustation, not papyrus. Sampling the identical frame uniformly at random instead gives separability 0.564 vs the picker's 0.168, median ratio 2.95×, random higher in 14 of 14 scrolls, Mann-Whitney p=5.4e-25. The flagship index's reference class silently contains something other than what it names — which is, verbatim, the trap the §4.3 ledger says this project caught five times. It is not in the report, and the report ships the repo that contains it. (b) Its anchor is soft: PHerc0139 carries a residual noise reference, and re-referencing the index's own three ROIs against the K2 audit's clean 128³ air window puts it at ~20.6, inside the degraded tier — which collapses the §1.5 anchor argument that three of the five degraded scrolls sit "1.6-4.6× below" the calibrator. (c) §1.7 concedes the index does not measure segmentability, does not predict readability, and §4.5 concedes bandwidth is "demonstrably not the readability axis." A judge is left asking what decision it actually informs, and the honest answer — a rescan priority list — is a recommendation to a team that controls beamtime and did not ask for one.
judges.what_a_hostile_reviewer_attacks_first:
"You screened every published Grand-Prize segment and found nothing. But by your own index the three scrolls you screened rank 8, 13 and 14 of 14; 23 of the 65 surfaces are z_dbg_gen_* debug dumps rather than curated segments; 18 place part of their surface outside the reconstructed volume; and you state yourself that only PHerc1203 was ever a fair test. You screened the scrolls your own first deliverable told us not to bother with. What did I learn that I did not already believe?" The report volunteers this in §2.7 and Limitation 2, which blunts the hit but does not dissolve it — and volunteering it four times over makes the reviewer's argument for him.

The deeper attack, which a careful reviewer reaches second and which is harder to answer: the five deliverables never connect. Index says look at PHerc0813 (rank 1). Instrument is validated and works. Corpus screen cannot reach 0813 because it has no published surface. §2.9 grows the first surfaces on 0813 — and the author's own alignment measurement (67.3° median to the local sheet normal, 0 of 8 within 30°, versus 14.6° and 7 of 9 for published meshes, Mann-Whitney p=0.00078) says they sample across the lamellae and average the modulation away. The report currently reports this as "not yet demonstrated to be tracking a lamella" with a ≈$0.70 gate pending, which reads as an unfinished promise rather than a diagnosed cause. Every arrow points at a target the work never hit.

Third, and cheapest for the reviewer: §2.2's positive control. w035 is listed in ink_9um's own labeled training corpus in both manifests (meta/ink9um_corpus.md) and is not one of the three segments the released checkpoints report validation metrics on. AUC 0.9991 is an on-training-data score. The exec summary calls it "an independent reproduction of that community result." The labels are human so nothing is circular, and the honest framing is barely weaker — but a reviewer who knows the corpus finds this in thirty seconds, and it is the foundation the entire unread-scroll lane rests on.
concrete_changes_ranked: SHIP THE PUBLIC REPO. git init trackD, MIT LICENSE, DATA_LICENSE.md, README, push, URL in the report. There is currently no .git anywhere in the tree and no LICENSE file — Ben's own BEN_TODO A6 calls this a hard eligibility requirement, and it is the one item on this list where failure means the submission is not scored rather than scored low. While doing it: exclude runpod/{fleet,survey_fleet,grow_pod,probe_pod}.json (live pod IDs and public IPs) and hunt/{mesh,corpus}cache/ (38 MB of redistributed scroll geometry, which contradicts the report's own 'redistributes no bulk scroll data' line). ~1-2 hours, and nothing else on this list matters if it does not happen.

BEN WRITES EVERY [BEN:] BLOCK IN HIS OWN VOICE, INCLUDING THE AI-ASSISTANCE DISCLOSURE. Title, opening framing, four per-section motivation sentences, two closing claims, the closing paragraph. The stated prize bar is that work arises from a HUMAN pursuing the project's goals, and villa's CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly closes LLM contributions lacking human commentary. A judge who opens this document and sees unfilled brackets addressed to the author by an agent will stop reading and will be right to. Disclosure volunteered reads infinitely better than disclosure discovered. The closing paragraph — what you want to do next, and the offer to run the battery on any segment the team names — is, on the evidence of past winners, the highest-response paragraph in the whole submission. ~2 hours.

POST THE THREE COMMUNITY DRAFTS NOW, NOT ON AUG 30. Adoption is explicitly prize-weighted and the July results show adopted tools outscore existing tools. Thirteen days is enough for two or three 'I ran this on X' replies, and one of those quoted in the submission is worth more than any further analysis you could run. Fix Post 1 first: it says 'five papyrus ROIs per scroll' (it is 2-5, median 4) and claims every volume was measured against an air reference (PHerc0139, the anchor the same post names, is residual-referenced). Lead the posting order with the renderer, not the index — the renderer is the thing someone else can use tomorrow, and the index is the thing you are least sure of.

FOLD THE k2c SEPARABILITY AXIS AND THE ROI-PICKER CORRECTION INTO §1, OR CUT §1's CLAIMS BACK TO WHAT SURVIVES. This is both the largest vulnerability and the largest untapped asset, and it is already computed: 168 cubes, 14 scrolls, 12 uniformly-random ROIs each; the control PHerc0139 ranks #1 of 14 at 0.748 [0.738, 0.775] against a 0.105 isotropic floor measured on 28 real in-scan air windows; Spearman ρ=+0.336 (p=0.24) with the K2b SNR, i.e. a genuinely orthogonal axis; ordering parameter-invariant at ρ=+0.967..+1.000 across block 16/32/64 and σ 0.5/1/2; the clipping confound refuted in the conservative direction; and the invalid phase-randomisation null found and removed with the reason stated. Alongside it, the picker bias: random 0.564 vs picked 0.168, ratio 2.95×, random higher in 14/14, p=5.4e-25. Shipping §1 without this, while the JSON sits in the repo you are handing the judges, is precisely the own-goal your own notes warn about — and 'I found the sampling bias in my own flagship deliverable, measured it at 14/14 scrolls, and published the corrected orthogonal axis' is a far stronger prize story than the index alone ever was. It also reorders your own next month: PHerc0358 is separability rank 2 and SNR rank 7, and is the target the corrected axis picks.

REWRITE §2.9 AND LIMITATION 4 AROUND THE 67.3° ROOT CAUSE, AND RETIRE THE PENDING ≈$0.70 GATE. Right now the report says the five on-material PHerc0813 patches are 'not yet demonstrated to be tracking a lamella' and leaves render+infer+battery as an unrun promise. Your own measurement says why: the patches sit at a median 67.3° to the local sheet normal, 0 of 8 within 30°, against 14.6° and 7 of 9 for published GP meshes (binomial p=2.2e-05, Mann-Whitney ours-vs-published p=0.00078), because vc_grow_seg_from_seed was run with no direction_fields and no normal_grid_path while the published pipeline guides growth with a structure-tensor normal field. That converts a soft 'it did not work yet' into a diagnosed tooling omission with a named fix — which is a contribution anyone growing surfaces can use, is a better §2.9 than the current one, and closes an open promise that BEN_TODO A8 already flags as a liability. Say plainly that the patches were withdrawn from the battery and why; do not render them.

FIX THE NUMERIC AND ATTRIBUTION ERRORS BEFORE ANYTHING SHIPS. In a report whose entire pitch is rigor, one of these found by a judge costs more than all of them cost to repair. In priority order: (a) §2.2/exec summary must disclose that w035 is in ink_9um's own labeled training corpus and is not among the three segments the checkpoints report validation on — AUC 0.9991 is an on-training-data score, so it bounds sensitivity rather than measuring it; (b) the exec summary credits the renderer with the 0.9991/0.9982 AUCs, which were measured on the published surface volume — the renderer's number is r=0.813, and that number has no JSON at all (add a ~15-line script emitting out/render_fidelity.json); (c) unique surfaces is 65 by name over all 80 rows, not 66 — your own report/scripts/corpus_summary.py prints 65 and a judge who runs the script you advertise will see it; (d) the tier gap is 2.97×, not 3.0×, and your own verify_report.py prints 2.97 while asserting only a 2.9-3.1 band; (e) the ledger is counted as ten, eleven and twelve in three places in one document; (f) the Paris 4 Gaussian expectation should be ~1,690 against the co-brightness-gated eligible n, not 8,488 against the ungated n — the conclusion survives at ~800×, the arithmetic as printed does not; (g) REPRODUCIBILITY §E's 'entire project $5.61' contradicts the exec summary's ≈$11 and has no corpus-survey line at all; (h) §3.2's '0.017 voxel residual translation' exists only as a comment in a docstring — no code computes it.

CUT THE FRONT MATTER TO TWO PAGES AND DEMOTE THE FIVE-MINUTE TABLE. 1,150 lines across seven files is more than a monthly-prize judge reads, and the exec summary is currently a wall of bolded numbers that the twelve-item limitations list immediately relitigates. What a judge should see in five minutes, in this order: the renderer and the gap it fills; the 80/80 screen at $5.5 with the 5-of-5-vs-0-of-71 discrimination; the ink_3d transfer diagnosis with its fine-tune recipe and the frozen 29,748-tile benchmark; the two acceptance gates. Everything else is appendix. The twelve-row table of questions-and-answers is doing the exec summary's job twice.

REFRAME LIMITATION 1 AND STATE THE §2.7 SCOPE BOUND ONCE. 'No ink was found, anywhere, by anything, in this work' is the result, not a limitation, and leading the list with it invites the judge to score the absence instead of the instrument. Move it into the framing where it belongs as scope discipline, and let Limitation 1 be the real first limitation. Then state the corpus bound once, in §2.7, and cross-reference it from the exec summary rather than restating it in the exec summary, the five-minute table and Limitation 2. Also add the one limitation the artifacts imply and the twelve omit: at 200 permutations the attainable p floor is 0.005, both the control and z_dbg_gen_00260 reach it, and Holm across 71 would demand p<7.0e-04 — so the hardened negative is carried by the shape gates, not by the significance test, which PROTOCOL_V2.md states plainly and the report does not.

judges.lens: Villa maintainer with a large tracker and no spare time, evaluating ONLY the reusable-tooling claims in REPORT.md's "Released artifacts" section: would any of this enter the toolchain, or would I reimplement it? I opened all ten tools, ran --help where one existed, traced every dependency, and checked what villa already has in-tree.
judges.verdict:
As a body of work this is strong — the writing, the negative results, and the self-correction discipline are all real. But the specific deliverable I was asked to judge ("reusable tooling," one of five headline deliverables and the entire pitch of §4.6) is largely not real, and it will take a maintainer about eleven minutes to establish that.

Hard facts I established by opening the files:

THERE IS NOTHING TO ADOPT FROM, TODAY. `trackD` is not a git repository. There is no README and no LICENSE anywhere under it (only villa's own third-party licenses one level up). REPORT.md's "All code MIT" is a statement about a repo that does not exist. Every adoption question below is currently moot; this is the first thing to fix and it is not optional.

ONLY 3 OF 10 TOOLS HAVE A COMMAND-LINE ENTRY POINT. `grep -l "argparse\|sys.argv"` across all ten returns exactly three: `render_tifxyz_sv.py`, `survey_segments.py`, `analyze_survey_corpus_v2.py`. The other seven are run by editing constants at the top of the file.

ONLY 2 OF 10 ARE PATH-CLEAN. Counting hard-coded `C:\`, `D:\`, or `/workspace/` literals per file: render_tifxyz_sv.py 0, corpus_summary.py 0 — and then verdict_common.py 2, verdict_* 1 each, qc_norm_equiv.py 5, qc_indomain_histmatch.py 4, check_air.py 3, vf_battery.py 4, survey_segments.py 10, analyze_survey_corpus_v2.py 2.

THE FLAGSHIP GATE POINTS AT A CLAUDE SESSION SCRATCHPAD. `qc_live/qc_norm_equiv.py:22` and `qc_indomain_histmatch.py` both open with `STUBS = r"C:\Users\benbl\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-benbl-Desktop-Vsuvious\b3441997-0118-49b2-8364-cbdf28fc6397\scratchpad\stubs"` followed by `sys.path.insert(0, STUBS)` — inserted AHEAD of villa. That directory holds hand-written fake `einops`, `huggingface_hub`, `timm`, `tqdm`, `nest_asyncio` modules and is not in the repo, cannot be regenerated, and is a per-session temp path. This is the "pre-fleet model acceptance gate," deliverable 5's headline reusable artifact. One line, and a reviewer knows nobody but the author has ever run this.

THE "~5-MIN/SEGMENT BATTERY" TAKES NO SEGMENT. `salvage/verdict_common.py` is a `MAPS` dict of thirteen hard-coded TIF filenames for two named PHerc1203 segments plus w035, at two hard-coded checkpoints (seed42/seed43 step-075000). `load_map(key)` takes a dict key, not a path. There is no way to point it at a segment. REPRODUCIBILITY.md §B.6 is honest about this ("Inputs: the 8 maps + control + labels"); REPORT.md's reuse bullet and COMMUNITY_POST's "turnkey / checkpoint-agnostic" are not. And the "pre-registered tripwire" that bullet promises is not in `salvage/verdict_*.py` at all — grep for `195` or `tripwire` there returns nothing; it lives in `runpod/survey_segments.py:22`.

THE AIR-CHECK GATE HAS NEVER RUN ON THE CORPUS IT IS CREDITED WITH. §4.6 item 7 says `hunt/check_air.py` "flags 18 of 66 published GP surfaces." `hunt/out/vertex_material.json` — the file check_air.py writes — has 10 rows. The 18-of-66 figure comes from `hunt/out/corpus_oob.json` (77 rows), a pure array-bounds comparison produced by a different script that reads no volume. check_air.py also has no argparse, `sys.path.insert`s a local villa source checkout, and requires a hand-curated `hunt/meshcache/segs.json` a stranger cannot construct.

THE FLAG-VERIFICATION "KIT" IS A CASE FILE. `verify_flag/vf_common.py:11` sets `FLAG = "z_dbg_gen_00166_inp_hr"` as a module constant; all thirteen `vf_*.py` inherit it. REPORT.md sells it as "given any screen hit, re-implement the screen's own statistic" — there is no "given any."

THE "MATCHED-NULL TEMPLATES" ARE NOT TEMPLATES. `comb/comb_skeptic_*.py` docstrings open "SKEPTIC PASS — flag 6 (K3 z~3900-4020 regional median-ratio elevation)", "flags 7 and 8", "flags 3, 4, 5". They are one-off passes against specific findings in this project.

ONE TOOL IS GENUINELY GOOD. `runpod/render_tifxyz_sv.py` — clean argparse (3 positionals, 7 defaulted options), zero hard-coded paths, imports only upstream villa APIs (`vesuvius.tifxyz`, `ink_detection.volume_io`, `label_zarr`, all from villa commit 960d76ac), writes the exact zarr-v2 layout `infer.py` consumes, includes the level-3 max-pool occupancy array so inference skips empty tiles, and has a recursive crop-splitting guard for the memory blowup. `--help` runs. ~110 lines. I would take this. But it was never sent as a PR, and the report never positions it against the three renderers already in villa: `tifxyz_label_transfer/self_render_tifxyz.py`, `ink_detection/preprocessing/prepare_9um_isotropic_input.py` (which produces exactly the 21-slice format, but only from an existing surface volume), and `volume-cartographer/apps/src/vc_render_tifxyz.cpp`. The gap it fills is real — tifxyz straight to a 21-slice SV with no published surface volume — but a maintainer's first question is "did he know about ours?", and nothing in the report answers it.

AND THE ONE THING A MAINTAINER WOULD ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT IS INVISIBLE. Four PRs and three issues against ScrollPrize/villa, all real, all authored by flummoxjr: #1487 fixes an inverted warp plus two more defects in SheetCompressionTransform; #1488 reports MemoryEfficientSoftDiceLoss exploding to ~1e13 and erasing BCE gradients; #1490 reports auxiliary_tasks silently training nothing with ZarrDataset; #1492 makes vesuvius.predict work with train_py checkpoints; #1479, #1480, #1489 round it out. These appear ZERO times in REPORT.md. They exist only in two passing parentheticals in the appendix and inside a `[BEN:]` bracket. For my lens these are worth more than all ten scripts combined, and they are buried.

The "pre-fleet model acceptance gate" (`qc_live/qc_*.py`), sold in the executive summary, in §4.6 item 1, and in COMMUNITY_POST post 2 as the flagship reusable artifact — "five tests, ≤30 tiles, ≈$0–1, checkpoint-agnostic, run it before you rent anything."

It is not a program. There is no runner, no argparse anywhere in the seven files, and no script that executes "the five tests"; they are seven separate scripts invoked by hand in an order documented nowhere. The report cannot even hold the list steady — §4.2 names one set of five, `round1_verdict.md` and §3.11 name a different set of five, and one of those five (tail discrimination) was computed on 3,346 tiles and structurally cannot run on 30.

Its actual inputs are not "30 tiles" in any portable sense: `qc_morph.py` and `qc_stats.py` glob `qc_live/round_1/w*_prob_*.npy` — 31 pre-pulled 21 MB of `.npy` from one specific fleet run at one specific set of coordinates, produced by `runpod/screen_band.py` on a six-pod fleet that no longer exists. `qc_norm_equiv.py` needs `D:\vesuvius-data\trackD\models\ink3d\ckpt_78k_fullsup.pth` as a module constant and a `smoke_1203_prob.npy` CLI reference region at origin (7281,7007,11615). The value here is entirely in `qc_live/round1_verdict.md` — the protocol, the scorecard, the reasoning about why an in-domain silent-tile control is the right acceptance criterion. That document is genuinely good and genuinely reusable by a human. The code beneath it is not reusable by anyone.
judges.what_a_hostile_reviewer_attacks_first:
They try to run one thing, and they pick the one the executive summary brags about.

The realistic sequence: reviewer reads "Two reusable acceptance gates come out of it: a ≤30-tile, ~$1 pre-fleet model gate." They look for the repo URL — there isn't one, and there is no git repo to make one from, no LICENSE, no README. Assume that gets fixed. They clone, `cd qc_live`, `head -25 qc_norm_equiv.py`, and hit:

    STUBS = r"C:\Users\benbl\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-benbl-Desktop-Vsuvious\b3441997-0118-49b2-8364-cbdf28fc6397\scratchpad\stubs"
    sys.path.insert(0, STUBS)

That is the attack. Not a statistics dispute — a path. It tells them in one glance that (a) this code has never been executed outside one machine, (b) it silently shadows real packages with hand-written fakes, and (c) the "checkpoint-agnostic, run it before you rent anything" claim two documents upstream was written without anyone checking whether the thing runs. In a report whose entire thesis is "we attacked our own claims before you had to," that single line is worth more to a hostile reviewer than any of the arithmetic errors, because it is a claim the author could have falsified in ten seconds and did not.

The second wave, once they are looking: `grep -rn "D:\\\\" trackD --include=*.py | wc -l` and `grep -rln argparse` on the ten reuse tools. 3 of 10 have entry points; 2 of 10 are path-clean. Then they check `hunt/out/vertex_material.json` against §4.6's "flags 18 of 66 surfaces" and find 10 rows. Then they grep `salvage/verdict_*.py` for the tripwire it is credited with and find nothing. Each of these is individually small; together they establish a pattern — the tooling section describes an intent, not an inventory — and that pattern is the one thing this submission cannot afford to have established about it, because the same reviewer will now go re-derive the statistics with the assumption that descriptions here are aspirational.

Third: they open REPRODUCIBILITY.md §B expecting invocations and find a script→inputs→outputs table with no command lines, and no entry at all for `survey_segments.py`, `segment_catalog.json`, `analyze_survey_corpus*.py`, `check_air.py`, or `verify_flag/vf_*` — five of the ten reuse tools, including the entire lane that produced deliverable 2.

What they will NOT attack, and this is worth knowing: `render_tifxyz_sv.py`. It survives inspection cleanly. If the tooling section were just that file plus the catalogue plus the provisioning script, there would be no attack surface here at all.
concrete_changes_ranked: 1. Create the repo. `git init` trackD, add MIT LICENSE, add a README, push public, put the URL in REPORT.md. Today there is no repository, no LICENSE, and no README — so every reuse claim in the document is unverifiable by construction, and 'All code MIT' describes nothing that exists. Nothing else on this list matters until this is done; a tooling claim with no repo behind it is not a weak claim, it is an absent one.

2. Delete the two `STUBS` lines. `qc_live/qc_norm_equiv.py:22` and `qc_live/qc_indomain_histmatch.py` both `sys.path.insert(0, ...)` a Claude-session temp scratchpad ahead of villa. synth.prize_verdict:
All three judges independently landed on **$2.5K**, which is a stronger signal than it looks — they reached it from three different directions and none was arguing the others' case. Where they genuinely disagree is on *what the deliverable is*, and that disagreement is the actionable part.

The hostile referee judges the content as $2.5K-worthy but says the delivery hands a reader the exact weapon the report claims immunity to — and he demonstrated it by puncturing the rigor claim three times in about forty minutes using only files the repo ships. His view: the corpus null is not the product; the instruments are.

The prize judge calibrates against the actual July 2026 record and makes the sharpest argument in the panel: an *ink-detection validation harness* — the closest historical analogue to this report's most reusable output — was priced at $1K, and failure-mode notebooks at $2.5K, while the $10K/$20K tier went exclusively to things that made the pipeline produce more (auto-meshing, annotation tooling, Khartes3D). Nothing here makes the pipeline produce one more mesh, one more label, or one more read letter. Measurement of this quality has an observed market price and it is $1K–$2.5K. He also names the structural problem no editing fixes: the five deliverables never close a loop — the index says look at PHerc0813, the instrument works, the corpus screen cannot reach 0813, and the surfaces grown on 0813 turned out oblique to the sheets. Every arrow points at a target the work never hit.

The villa maintainer is the most negative on the specific thing he was asked to judge and the most useful about it. His measurements: 3 of 10 "reuse tools" have a command-line entry point, 2 of 10 are path-clean, and two of the flagship gate's scripts `sys.path.insert` a Claude-session temp scratchpad *ahead of villa* — a per-session path that cannot be regenerated. His verdict is that this wins on the report, not the toolchain, and that the tooling section as written will read as overclaiming to anyone who checks. I spot-confirmed his central artifact-attribution findings (check_air.py's output has 10 rows, not 66; the tripwire lives in survey_segments.py, not salvage/verdict_*.py) and they hold.

They also disagree on the strongest element, and the spread is informative: the referee says the forward/reverse asymmetry statistic (and supplies the missing cross-render control, r = 0.094 both ways, closing the strongest structural objection to the headline); the prize judge says the v1→v2 self-correction round trip; the maintainer says none of the analysis — the segment catalogue, the 150 saved maps, and the provisioning recipe, explicitly ranked above both the tools and the conclusions.

My own view: **$2.5K, conditional on eligibility, with a real path to $5K and a live path to no_award.** I weight the prize judge's calibration most heavily because it is the only argument anchored in observed payouts rather than in impressions of quality. But I weight the maintainer's finding as the sharpest *correctable* risk: the reuse list is the one section where the report's own subtractive discipline was not applied, and cutting it from ten tools to four with the rest honestly relabelled as "method documents with reference implementations" is a subtraction that makes the submission stronger — the same move the report already makes well everywhere else. The no_award path is not about content at all: no repo, no LICENSE, 36 unfilled [BEN:] blocks including the title and the AI-assistance disclosure, submitted to a team whose CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly closes LLM contributions lacking human commentary. The $5K path runs through the community posts landing *now* with a week to accumulate replies, plus §1.8's separability axis and the ROI-picker correction folded in properly — "I found the sampling bias in my own flagship deliverable, measured it at 14/14 scrolls, and published the corrected orthogonal axis" is a materially better story than the index alone ever was, and it is already computed and sitting on disk.
